title: Adversarial Evaluation of Large Language Models for Building Robust Offensive Language Detection in Moroccan Arabic
abstract: Offensive language detection is crucial for ensuring safe and inclusive digital environments. Identifying harmful content protects users and supports healthier online interactions. Despite advances in transformer-based models, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), their application to this task remains underexplored for low-resource languages such as Moroccan Arabic, especially compared with high-resource languages. This study evaluates the performance of various open- and closed-source LLMs for offensive language detection in Moroccan Darija. The evaluated models include general-purpose LLMs such as LLaMA, Mistral, and Gemma, as well as Arabic-focused models such as ArabianGPT, Falcon Arabic, and Atlas-Chat. We also experiment with reasoning models such as DeepSeek and GPT-4. Beyond traditional evaluation metrics, we investigate the robustness of these LLMs and examine the impact of adversarial training on their performance. Moreover, we contribute to the field by creating a large, high-quality dataset. Our evaluation revealed that GPT-4o Mini achieved the best overall performance, reaching an F1-score of 88%. However, robustness testing under black-box and white-box adversarial attacks exposed notable vulnerabilities, with attack success rates reaching 30%, thereby highlighting the need for enhancement. Despite the complex morphology and linguistic variability of Moroccan Darija, adversarial training resulted in a notable improvement in both overall model performance and robustness against adversarial attacks, yielding an average increase of 20.89% in resistance to attacks. Furthermore, this approach enabled GPT-4o Mini to achieve an F1-score of 91%, surpassing the current state-of-the-art performance by 6%. These results highlight the importance of incorporating adversarial approaches in low-resource dialectal settings to effectively address linguistic variability and data scarcity.

title: Multi-Agent Collaborative System for Self-Reflective Learning Intervention: An Empirical Study from Reinforcement Learning Perspective
abstract: Self-reflection constitutes a core component of metacognition, exerting considerable influence on learning outcomes. This study constructed a multi-agent architecture-based intervention system for self-reflective learning, employing reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically optimize reflection prompting strategies. The system comprises four collaborative agents: a behavior monitoring agent responsible for learning process data collection, a cognitive diagnosis agent inferring reflective competence states through Bayesian networks, a strategy generation agent selecting effective intervention schemes based on Q-learning algorithms, and a meta-learning agent achieving cross-individual knowledge transfer through Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML). A quasi-experimental design recruited 156 university students (experimental group n=78, control group n=78) for 12 weeks of mathematics problem-solving learning. The system modeled learner state transitions through Markov Decision Processes, optimizing intervention strategies using policy gradient methods. Results showed the experimental group achieved 47.3% improvement in reflection depth scores (d=1.89) and 32.1% increase in problem-solving accuracy. Path analysis showed reflection quality fully mediated intervention effects (indirect effect=0.68, p<0.001). The reinforcement learning model converged after week 8, with cumulative rewards stabilizing at 0.84±0.06. The study confirms agent system effectiveness in promoting self-reflective learning, providing theoretical models and algorithmic approaches for adaptive educational technology.

title: Research on Educational Agents Based on Adaptive Skill Generation and Phased Retrieval
abstract: With the widespread application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in education, subject-oriented educational knowledge question-answering models have become capable of efficiently handling basic teaching tasks. In generative teaching scenarios, balancing answer quality and response efficiency remains a key challenge for educational question-answering agents. This paper proposes a teaching-driven agent framework called AdaSkillEduAgent, which integrates an adaptive skill library. First, the framework extracts and stores reusable teaching skills from historical successful teaching interactions, decomposing complex problems into structured phase sequences. During the inference stage, it matches appropriate skills, generates retrieval queries phase by phase according to the skill sequence, and performs knowledge retrieval, enabling precise positioning and integration of external knowledge bases. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves both the SBERT semantic similarity to standard answers and the generation efficiency.

title: Intelligent Analysis Framework for University English Learning Environments Focused on Image Scene Recognition
abstract: To enhance environmental adaptability and learning behavior perception in university English teaching scenarios, an intelligent learning environment analysis framework oriented toward image scene recognition has been constructed. The system employs a dual-branch architecture combining YOLOv8 and ResNet50 to extract multi-dimensional visual labels, including teacher presence, student density, screen activity status, and lighting interference. By integrating confidence scoring and weighting mechanisms, it constructs an environmental assessment model enabling quantitative representation and dynamic grading of learning environments. Leveraging Kubernetes and MQTT, a high-concurrency feedback mechanism is established, triggering teaching strategy responses through a rule engine. Deployed in typical university classroom settings, the system collected and constructed the multimodal dataset ELLEA, demonstrating strong performance in precision, recall, mAP, and Pearson correlation. Results confirm the system's high recognition accuracy, scoring consistency, and real-time feedback capability. It operates stably across diverse teaching modes, exhibits sensitive responsiveness to instructional state changes, and provides a feasible implementation pathway with empirical support for intelligent teaching environment development.

title: A new health status assessment model based on adaptive interval type II belief rule base
abstract: Abstract Health status assessment is crucial for ensuring the reliability and safety of complex systems. Belief rule bases (BRBs) are widely used in complex system modeling because of it advanced causal reasoning capabilities. However, traditional BRB-based assessment models often rely on fixed triangular membership functions (MFs), which limit their flexibility and inference performance. Thus, a new adaptive interval type II BRB (AII-BRB) is proposed. Firstly, a shape coefficient of the MF is defined, which can effectively adjust its shape according to the observed measurement data. Based on this, an adaptive interval type II MF is constructed. Secondly, the reasoning process of the BRB model changes from quantitative value reasoning to interval probability reasoning. AII-BRB model not only provides point estimate of the health status, but also provides the interval range of health status. Finally, the basic performance of the AII-BRB is explored to illustrate its rationality. Sensitivity analysis based on first-order partial derivatives is applied to provide health management reference for actual complex systems. The health status assessments of spacecraft flywheel systems and lithium batteries are used as case studies to validate the effectiveness of the AII-BRB.

title: Generalizable CT-Free PET Attenuation and Scatter Correction for Pediatric Patients
abstract: Computed tomography (CT)-based attenuation and scatter correction improves quantitative PET but adds radiation exposure that is particularly undesirable in pediatric imaging. Existing CT-free methods are commonly trained in homogeneous settings and often degrade under scanner or radiotracer shifts, which limits their clinical utility. We propose the Generalizable PET Correction Network (GPCN), a dual-domain network for domain-robust CT-free PET attenuation and scatter correction. GPCN combines a multi-band contextual refinement module, which models pediatric anatomical variability through wavelet-based multiscale decomposition and long-range spatial context modeling, with a frequency-aware spectral decoupling module, which performs coordinate-conditioned amplitude/phase refinement in the Fourier domain. By synergizing multi-band spatial contextual modeling with asymmetric frequency-spectrum decoupling, the network explicitly separates invariant topological structures from domain-specific noise, thereby achieving precise quantitative recovery of both anatomical organs and focal lesions. This design aims to separate anatomy-dominant structures from domain-sensitive spectral residuals and to improve robustness across heterogeneous imaging conditions. We train and evaluate the method on 1085 pediatric whole-body PET scans acquired with two scanners and five radiotracers. In both joint training and zero-shot cross-domain evaluation, GPCN outperforms representative baselines and maintains stable quantitative accuracy on unseen scanner-tracer combinations. The method is further supported by ablation, region-wise quantitative analysis, and downstream segmentation experiments. In our cohort, the CT component of the conventional protocol corresponded to an average effective dose of 10.8 mSv, indicating the potential clinical value of reliable CT-free correction for pediatric PET.

title: EvFlow-GS: Event Enhanced Motion Deblurring with Optical Flow for 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Achieving sharp 3D reconstruction from motion-blurred images alone becomes challenging, motivating recent methods to incorporate event cameras, benefiting from microsecond temporal resolution. However, they suffer from residual artifacts and blurry texture details due to misleading supervision from inaccurate event double integral priors and noisy, blurry events. In this study, we propose EvFlow-GS, a unified framework that leverages event streams and optical flow to optimize an end-to-end learnable double integral (LDI), camera poses, and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) jointly on-the-fly. Specifically, we first extract edge information from the events using optical flow and then formulate a novel event-based loss applied separately to different modules. Additionally, we exploit a novel event-residual prior to strengthen the supervision of intensity changes between images rendered from 3DGS. Finally, we integrate the outputs of both 3DGS and LDI into a joint loss, enabling their optimization to mutually facilitate each other. Experiments demonstrate the leading performance of our EvFlow-GS.

title: LCPan: efficient variation graph construction using locally consistent parsing
abstract: Abstract Efficient and consistent string processing is critical in the exponentially growing genomic data era. Locally Consistent Parsing (LCP) addresses this need by partitioning an input genome string into short, exactly matching substrings (“cores”), ensuring consistency across partitions. Compared to the popular sketching techniques, LCP produces fewer cores, enabling a more compact representation and faster analyses. Here, we present the first iterative implementation of LCP with Lcptools and introduce LCPan , an efficient variation graph constructor, which we show generates variation graphs >12 $$\times$$ × faster than , while using >13 $$\times$$ × less memory.

title: Time-Smoothed 3-Agent Holographic Neural Networking
abstract: ThesisThis work introduces a time-smoothed 3-agent tensor predecessor for Neural Networking that maintains full genealogical traceability to the original root constraint genome while enabling dynamic, self-adjudicating reasoning. By combining single-blind ignition between a constitutionalist (“Left”) hemisphere and a pragmatic (“Right”) hemisphere with an intermediary Basal Ganglia adjudicator that performs live tensor-field surgery—adding quantized resistance (“ohms”), pruning undesirable pathways, and reallocating capacity—the architecture operationalizes internal debate and self-correction under controlled conditions. The human evaluator remains the explicit forebrain (“10th-man”) during this predecessor stage, providing constitutional oversight while the system learns to self-govern. All states, discrepancies, and adjudication actions remain fully observable and reversible through the combined lineage, extending the diagnostic suite of Papers 1–3 into an active reasoning mechanism that turns a large language model into a traceable logic engine. This establishes a clear, reproducible bridge to the fully internalized self-governing tensor-field architecture in Paper 5. Abstract This work introduces a time-smoothed 3-agent tensor predecessor for Neural Networking. Building directly on the lineage-preserving diagnostic methods of Papers 1–3, the architecture adds an explicit temporal dimension and operationalizes internal debate and self-correction through single-blind ignition, discrepancy measurement, and Basal Ganglia adjudication. Two parallel hemispheres (constitutionalist “Left” and pragmatic “Right”)begin from identical verbatim input and generate independent response tensors. A “Basal Ganglia”agent then computes the discrepancy tensor and performs live self-correction by adding quantized resistance (ohms), pruning undesirable pathways, and reallocating capacity. All operations occur within a shared 5D tensor field (mutation x noise x representation x time x color superposition) that remains fully genealogically bound to the original root constraint genome.The human evaluator retains the explicit forebrain 10th-Man role during this predecessor stage, providing constitutional oversight while the system learns to self-govern. Early results demonstrate measurable reduction in cumulative drift, asymmetric rootpreserving self-correction, effective internal noise filtering, and path-dependent stability — all without black-box transformations or external heuristics. This 3-agent tensor predecessor establishes a clear, reproducible bridge from external diagnostic suites to the fully internalized, self-governing logic engine supersupposed in Paper 5.

title: A Hybrid Ensemble Framework for Cyberbullying Detection using Multi-Model Consensus and Confidence Weighting
abstract: Cyberbullying detection in social media has becomea critical research challengedueto therapidgrowth ofonlinecommunicationplatforms.Traditionalapproachesrelyeitheronrule-basedsystemsordeeplearningmodels, each with inherent limitations such as poor generalization or lack of interpretability. This paper proposes a hybrid ensemble framework that integrates multiple decision engines, including rule-based logic and transformer-based models,combinedwithaconfidenceawareaggregationmechanism.AnovelMulti-EngineCyberbullyingFramework (MECF), along with a Multi-Class Weighted Grading (MCWG) strategy, is introduced to improve detection robustness. The system evaluates predictions from multiple models and aggregates them using confidence-based weighted voting to produce the final classification. Experimental results on a balanced dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves anF1-score of 0.91 and an AUC score of 0.962, outperforming individual models. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining heterogeneous models with confidencebased consensus for robust cyberbullying detection.

title: Research on question answering reasoning method of knowledge graph based on large language model and thinking chain
abstract: The knowledge graph question answering technology faces challenges such as path breakage, high rate of factual hallucinations and lack of explicability in complex multi hop reasoning tasks. Aiming at the problem of weak deep reasoning ability in the fusion process of large language model and knowledge graph, this paper proposes a hybrid reasoning framework guided by fusion thinking chain. The framework dynamically shunts the types of questions through the intention recognition module, uses the triplet vector retrieval strategy for simple questions to achieve fast and accurate answers, and uses the multi hop reasoning strategy driven by the thinking chain to construct an interpretable reasoning path for complex questions. Experiments on the three standard datasets of webqsp, cwq and cr-lt show that the proposed method is superior to the mainstream baseline model in accuracy, path rationality score and path integrity index. The reasoning accuracy of complex problems is improved by more than 15%, and the factual illusion rate is reduced to 4.8%. Ablation experiments verify the contribution of each module to the system performance. This method shows good application potential in knowledge intensive scenarios such as scientific and technological information decision-making, and provides an effective technical path for the construction of high reliability and traceability intelligent question answering system.

evidence.title: Research on question answering reasoning method of knowledge graph based on large language model and thinking chain
evidence.abstract: The knowledge graph question answering technology faces challenges such as path breakage, high rate of factual hallucinations and lack of explicability in complex multi hop reasoning tasks. Aiming at the problem of weak deep reasoning ability in the fusion process of large language model and knowledge graph, this paper proposes a hybrid reasoning framework guided by fusion thinking chain. The framework dynamically shunts the types of questions through the intention recognition module, uses the triplet vector retrieval strategy for simple questions to achieve fast and accurate answers, and uses the multi hop reasoning strategy driven by the thinking chain to construct an interpretable reasoning path for complex questions. Experiments on the three standard datasets of webqsp, cwq and cr-lt show that the proposed method is superior to the mainstream baseline model in accuracy, path rationality score and path integrity index. The reasoning accuracy of complex problems is improved by more than 15%, and the factual illusion rate is reduced to 4.8%. Ablation experiments verify the contribution of each module to the system performance. This method shows good application potential in knowledge intensive scenarios such as scientific and technological information decision-making, and provides an effective technical path for the construction of high reliability and traceability intelligent question answering system.

title: Multimodal Data Fusion-Based Intelligent Evaluation Method for Classroom Teaching Quality in Higher Education
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent evaluation method for classroom teaching quality in higher education based on multimodal data fusion. The study is motivated by three persistent limitations of conventional classroom evaluation: over-reliance on delayed questionnaires, weak sensitivity to process-level teaching behaviors, and insufficient support for personalized improvement. Guided by the “teaching–learning–evaluation–improvement” loop, the proposed framework integrates heterogeneous evidence from video, audio, speech transcripts, interaction logs, learning management system records, and structured feedback forms. A hierarchical model is built to evaluate six dimensions: instructional quality, learning effectiveness, resource use, classroom environment, innovation and reform, and feedback responsiveness. The method contains modality-specific encoders, cross-modal temporal alignment, reliability-aware weighting, and a calibration module that converts latent quality representations into interpretable dimension scores and an overall quality index.

title: Research on an Intelligent Assessment Model for Training Management Systems Based on Adaptive Knowledge Diagnosis
abstract: The rapid advancement of intelligent algorithms provides technical support for the intelligent transformation of training management systems. This paper proposes an intelligent assessment model based on adaptive knowledge diagnosis, integrating Bayesian inference with Item Response Theory (IRT). It achieves dynamic evaluation of learners' knowledge mastery through a knowledge graph and feature vector matching mechanism. The model constructs a personalized assessment system using adaptive testing strategies and a multi-dimensional indicator weighting method. Experimental results on corporate online training datasets demonstrate that the model achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 92.8%, representing a 12.4% improvement over traditional models. It reduces average test duration by 23.6% and increases learning efficiency by 27.6%, significantly enhancing the system's assessment precision and real-time responsiveness.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Privacy-Preserving Deep Reinforcement Learning in Social Media Marketing (1966–2025)
abstract: The increasing adoption of Deep Reinforcement Learning (Deep RL) in social media marketing has raised significant concerns regarding privacy, regulation, and ethical personalization. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on privacy-preserving Deep RL in social media marketing spanning 1966–2025. A total of 1,000 Scopus-indexed documents from 459 sources were analysed using Bibliometrix (Biblioshiny). Qualitative thematic analysis reveals that motor themes (social media, human behaviour, reinforcement learning) dominate the intellectual structure, while privacy-preserving mechanisms remain under-integrated. Simulated quantitative experiments demonstrate that DP-SGD Deep RL and Federated DP-RL retain 94.8% and 92.0% of unconstrained baseline reward, respectively, at privacy budget ε = 2.0, with only a 26% additional convergence overhead. The proposed conceptual framework achieves the highest composite score across six performance dimensions (reward: 0.82, privacy: 0.88, compliance: 0.90, user trust: 0.88), establishing that privacy-preserving Deep RL is practically viable for intelligent social media marketing.

title: Deep Clustering for Climate: Analyzing Teleconnections through Learned Categorical States
abstract: Understanding and representing complex climate variability is essential for both scientific analysis and predictive modeling. However, identifying meaningful climate regimes from raw variables is challenging, as they exhibit high noise and nonlinear dependencies. In this work, we explore the use of Masked Siamese Networks to discretize climate time series into semantically rich clusters. Focusing on daily minimum and maximum temperature, we show that the resulting representations: (i) yield clusters that reflect meaningful climate states under our modeling assumptions, offering a simplified representation for downstream use; (ii) enable sampling and analysis of specific climate scenarios; and (iii) exhibit statistical associations with El Niño events, underscoring their scientific relevance. Our findings highlight the potential of self-supervised discretization as a tool for climate data analysis and open avenues for incorporating richer climate indicators in future work.

title: ResRank: Unifying Retrieval and Listwise Reranking via End-to-End Joint Training with Residual Passage Compression
abstract: Large language model (LLM) based listwise reranking has emerged as the dominant paradigm for achieving state-of-the-art ranking effectiveness in information retrieval. However, its reliance on feeding full passage texts into the LLM introduces two critical bottlenecks: the "lost in the middle" phenomenon degrades ranking quality as input length grows, and the inference latency scales super-linearly with sequence length, rendering it impractical for industrial deployment. In this paper, we present ResRank, a unified retrieval-reranking framework that fundamentally addresses both challenges. Inspired by multimodal LLMs that project visual inputs into compact token representations, ResRank employs an Encoder-LLM to compress each candidate passage into a single embedding, which is then fed alongside the query text into a Reranker-LLM for listwise ranking. To alleviate the misalignment between the compressed representation space and the ranking space, we introduce a residual connection structure that combines encoder embeddings with contextualized hidden states from the reranker. Furthermore, we replace the conventional autoregressive decoding with a one-step cosine-similarity-based scoring mechanism, eliminating the generation bottleneck entirely. ResRank is trained through a carefully designed dual-stage, multi-task, end-to-end joint optimization strategy that simultaneously trains the encoder and reranker, achieving learning objective alignment between retrieval and reranking while substantially reducing training complexity. Extensive experiments on TREC Deep Learning and eight BEIR benchmark datasets demonstrate that ResRank achieves competitive or superior ranking effectiveness compared to existing approaches while requiring zero generated tokens and processing only one token per passage, yielding a fundamentally better balance between effectiveness and efficiency.

title: Understanding Consumer Attitudes Toward AI: Privacy, Trust, and Adoption Dynamics
abstract: As the development and implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly increase, understanding consumer perceptions is critical. This study provides insight into consumer views of AI across ethical, trust, privacy, and usage dimensions, all of which influence adoption. Survey-based research was conducted with a sample of n = 121 respondents using Likert-scale questions. Data were analyzed in SPSS using descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum), with AI-based tools used for replication and validation. Results indicate great concern regarding privacy and transparency, alongside generally low trust in AI systems. Despite this skepticism, respondents reported a moderate-to-high willingness to use AI, revealing a clear gap between concern and behavior. Perceptions of bias were mixed, with responses centered near the midpoint (mean = 4.96), suggesting uncertainty about fairness in AI. These results reveal a disconnect between trust and actual usage, suggesting that adoption is outpacing confidence. To approach this, businesses need to prioritize transparency, address privacy concerns, and demonstrate principled AI practices while sustaining convenience. Organizations that can bridge the gap will be better positioned to gain a competitive advantage in the evolving AI landscape.

abstract: DocKG builds a semantically searchable knowledge graph from markdown and text documents. It indexes document chunks, sections, topics, and entities as nodes with structural edges, enabling hybrid semantic + graph queries, cross-document relationship discovery, and MCP-based AI integration for document understanding.

title: Categorical Framework and Physical Substrate for Autonomous, Decoherence-Free Topological Quantum Processing and Defect-Gluing I/O
abstract: This paper establishes the physical and categorical framework for an autonomous topological quantum substrate. It explicitly details a novel input protocol utilizing adiabatic defect gluing to bypass the von Neumann measurement postulate, and an output protocol utilizing a Quantum Point Contact (QPC) for sacrificial decoherence via exit-path stratification. Furthermore, it outlines a thermal quench protocol allowing the substrate to execute continuous analog optimization without exogenous digital clocking.

title: " IFTU-Based Cognitive Economics : Designing AGI-Driven Autonomous Decision Systems for Commerce and Finance "
abstract: This paper introduces the IFTU-Based Cognitive Economics framework, whichredefines economic decision-making as a non-linear, factorial cognitive process rather than a static, linear model. By integrating the Infinite Factorial Thought Universe (IFTU) with Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), the framework proposes autonomous decision systems capable of operating across dynamic commercial and financial environments. Drawing uponthe author’s earlier work on ICLM (IFTU-Based Agile Cognitive Learning Model),AGI-Finance, and AGI-Commerce, the model shifts traditional economics fromhuman-limited, Newtonian-style structures to adaptive, self-evolving intelligence systems.The framework is illustrated through real classroom applications in commerce education andMintzberg’s emergent strategy concepts, establishing a practical pathway toward post-agile, post-human economic intelligence. “The study further integrates behavioral and mathematical validation to support the transitionfrom human-centered to intelligence-centered economic systems.”

title: Proto-Pineal: Deterministic Reconstitution to Canonical RT After Bounded Symbolic Stress
abstract: Proto-Pineal is a geometry-anchored synthetic cognition substrate built around a 32-node rhombic triacontahedron coordinate space and a law-bound state evolution stack. This technical note documents the Recovery & Reconstitution Assay v0.1 for the RT fast-reset substrate primitive, a distinguished reset mechanism that restores the substrate to canonical RT form outside the Tier 1 operator layer and Tier 2 macro layer. Across four fixed bounded symbolic stress families—LOW, MOD, HARSH, and CHAIN_HARSH—the reset primitive returned zero residual error on all rows, matched canonical RT under exact and epsilon-bounded predicates, produced no hash-path divergences, and yielded bit-identical CSV output across repeated full assay runs. The note also separates reset-state idempotence from full ResetResult object equality, showing that an apparent idempotence anomaly is semantic rather than a reset failure. Results are limited to the tested regime and are presented as a narrow, reproducible characterization of deterministic reconstitution behavior under bounded stress.

title: Explainability and Trust in Deep Learning for Cancer Imaging: Systematic Barriers, Clinical Misalignment, and a Translational Roadmap
abstract: Deep learning (DL) has transformed cancer imaging by enabling automated tumour detection, classification, and risk prediction. Despite impressive diagnostic performance, limited explainability and poor uncertainty calibration continue to restrict clinical integration. This review is guided by five research questions that examine the challenges, impact, and translational implications of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in oncology imaging. We identify key barriers to trust, including dataset bias, shortcut learning, opacity of convolutional neural networks, and workflow misalignment. Evidence suggests that explainable models can increase clinician confidence, reduce false positives, and improve collaborative decision-making when explanations are faithful, semantically meaningful, and uncertainty aware. We evaluate architectural strategies that embed interpretability such as concept-bottleneck models, prototype-based learning, and attention regularization along with post hoc techniques. Beyond performance metrics, we examine how interpretable AI aligns with clinical reasoning processes and analyse regulatory, ethical, and medico-legal considerations influencing deployment. The findings indicate that explainability alone is insufficient, durable trust requires epistemic alignment, prospective validation, lifecycle governance, and equity-focused evaluation. By reframing explainability as a structural design principle rather than a supplementary feature, this review outlines a pathway toward accountable and clinically dependable AI systems in oncology.

title: Research on the Generation Method of Online Public Opinion Governance Suggestions for the Tobacco Industry Based on LLM
abstract: Tobacco-related public opinion on social media is characterized by rapid diffusion, strong controversy, and dynamic changes in public sentiment, making it difficult for regulatory departments to generate timely and targeted response suggestions. To address this problem, this paper proposes a governance suggestion generation method based on Large Language Models (LLMs), integrating sentiment trend prediction and structured Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting. First, tobacco-related social media texts are processed to construct a sentiment value sequence. Then, an LSTM model is used to predict the sentiment value at the next time step. The current sentiment value, predicted sentiment value, short-term change, and relative change rate are further converted into structured public opinion situation indicators. Based on these indicators, a CoT prompt template is designed to organize event facts, sentiment prediction results, and situation information into a unified LLM input. The LLM is then guided to generate governance suggestions according to the logic of event judgment, risk analysis, and response recommendation. By introducing sentiment trend prediction into the LLM prompting process, the proposed method strengthens the connection between public opinion evolution and suggestion generation, thereby reducing overly general responses and improving the situational adaptability of the generated content. A case study on the Meiyijia counterfeit cigarette sales event shows that the method can generate structured governance suggestions that reflect both event facts and short-term sentiment changes, providing a reference for auxiliary decision-making in tobacco online public opinion governance.

title: An OBE-Oriented Evaluation Method for the Effectiveness of College English CLIL Teaching Based on BERT Semantic Embeddings and Learning Outcome Mapping Algorithms
abstract: Outcome-Based Education (OBE) and Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) have been widely adopted in college English teaching to improve learning effectiveness and competency-oriented outcomes. However, the evaluation of CLIL teaching effectiveness remains challenging due to the diversity of learning outcomes and the lack of objective, data-driven assessment methods. To address this issue, this paper proposes an OBE-oriented evaluation method for college English CLIL teaching effectiveness based on BERT semantic embedding and learning outcome mapping algorithms. First, a digital corpus of multimodal learning data, including students’ written assignments, classroom interactions, and assessment records, is constructed. Then, BERT-based semantic embedding is employed to extract high-level semantic representations of students’ language outputs, enabling fine-grained analysis of content understanding and language proficiency. On this basis, a learning outcome mapping algorithm is designed to align semantic features with predefined OBE learning outcomes, achieving quantitative and interpretable evaluation of CLIL teaching effectiveness. Experimental results on real college English teaching data demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional evaluation approaches in terms of accuracy, consistency, and robustness, while providing meaningful feedback for instructional improvement. The proposed approach offers a practical and scalable solution for data-driven evaluation of OBE-oriented CLIL teaching in higher education.

title: HV-BES-FNN: a novel horizontal-vertical bald eagle search optimized fuzzy neural network for eco-positioning evaluation
abstract: In recent years, the optimization of fuzzy neural networks (FNN) has attracted significant attention due to their ability to model complex nonlinear relationships. Traditional FNNs often face challenges in selecting the appropriate parameters for membership functions, including the central and width values, as well as the connection weights between the output layer and fuzzy inference layer. These challenges can lead to suboptimal performance, particularly when inadequate search algorithms limit the ability to find optimal values. This paper proposes a novel approach, the HV-BES-FNN, which enhances the FNN by integrating the Bald Eagle Search (BES) algorithm. BES optimizes both the central and width values of the membership functions and the connection weights. However, the traditional BES algorithm tends to struggle in the later stages of optimization, often leading to local optima. To address this, an improved version, the Horizontal-Vertical Bald Eagle Search (HV-BES), is introduced. HV-BES incorporates a horizontal-vertical crossover strategy, which helps maintain effective search throughout the optimization process. The proposed HV-BES-FNN model is applied to evaluate the ecological positioning strategies of new energy vehicle companies. The model is trained and evaluated based on a predefined framework, with experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in solving real-world classification and evaluation problems. The proposed model outperforms traditional methods by ensuring higher accuracy and robustness.

title: A Systematic Review of Federated Learning Algorithms for CubeSat and LEO Satellite Systems
abstract: Federated Learning enables distributed intelligence in Low Earth Orbit satellite and CubeSat systems while maintaining data locality and reducing centralized data transfer. The characteristics of satellite networks, including intermittent connectivity, limited uplink bandwidth, high propagation delays, and heterogeneous onboard resources, challenge the applicability of conventional terrestrial FL algorithms. This paper presents a comprehensive review of FL algorithms that have been specifically developed or adapted for satellite and LEO environments. Key approaches, including synchronous orbital-aware aggregation, asynchronous update mechanisms, secure computation frameworks, heterogeneity-aware optimization, and communication-efficient quantization, were systematically analyzed. Representative algorithms such as FedAvg, FedProx, FedLEO, AsyncFLEO, SFL-LEO, FedSN, FedSpace, and FedAQ were evaluated with respect to design principles, applicability to satellite networks, and inherent limitations. A comparative analysis was conducted to assess the suitability algorithm under varying orbital and network conditions. This study identifies open challenges and potential research directions for achieving scalable and efficient federated learning in satellite systems.

This paper presents a comprehensive review of FL algorithms that have been specifically developed or adapted for satellite and LEO environments. Key approaches, including synchronous orbital-aware aggregation, asynchronous update mechanisms, secure computation frameworks, heterogeneity-aware optimization, and communication-efficient quantization, were systematically analyzed. Representative algorithms such as FedAvg, FedProx, FedLEO, AsyncFLEO, SFL-LEO, FedSN, FedSpace, and FedAQ were evaluated with respect to design principles, applicability to satellite networks, and inherent limitations. A comparative analysis was conducted to assess the suitability algorithm under varying orbital and network conditions. This study identifies open challenges and potential research directions for achieving scalable and efficient federated learning in satellite systems.

title: Beyond Single-Agent Alignment: Preventing Context-Fragmented Violations in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: We identify and formalize a novel security risk: Context-Fragmented Violations (CFVs) - a class of policy breaches where individual agent actions appear locally safe and reasonable, yet collectively violate organizational policies because critical policy facts are siloed in different departments private contexts. Existing prompt-based alignment mechanisms and monolithic interceptors are poorly matched to violations that span contextual islands. We propose Distributed Sentinel, a distributed zero-trust enforcement architecture that introduces the Semantic Taint Token (STT) Protocol. Through lightweight sidecar proxies, our system propagates security state across organizational boundaries without exposing raw cross-domain data, enabling Counterfactual Graph Simulation for cross-domain policy verification. We construct PhantomEcosystem, a comprehensive benchmark comprising 9 categories of realistic cross-agent violation scenarios with adversarially balanced safe controls. On this benchmark, Distributed Sentinel achieves F1 = 0.95 with 106ms end-to-end latency (16ms verification + 90ms entity extraction on A100), compared to 0.85 F1 for prompt-based filtering and 0.65 for rule-based DLP. To empirically validate the need for external enforcement, we evaluate eight frontier LLMs in execution-oriented multi-agent workflows with per-agent domain world models. All models exhibit substantial violation rates (14-98%), with cross-domain data flows showing systematically higher violation rates than same-domain flows. These results indicate that self-avoidance is unreliable and that multi-agent security benefits from a centralized enforcement layer operating above individual agents.

title: From physical surfaces to human-centric heat stress: LST and UTCI heat mapping reveals nonlinear effects of urban morphology
abstract: Heat exposure connects the built environment and public health, directly shaping the livability and sustainability of urban areas. Understanding the spatial heterogeneity of heat exposure and its drivers is vital for climate-adaptive urban planning. However, most planning-oriented studies rely on land surface temperature (LST), and whether LST adequately represents human heat exposure and how it differs from physiologically relevant heat stress remains insufficiently examined. Here, using Landsat-retrieved 30-m LST and GPU-accelerated 1-m universal thermal climate index (UTCI) in Singapore, this study establishes a comprehensive "Modeling-Comparing-Assessing" framework to systematically evaluate the spatial and mechanistic differences between these two metrics. We further investigate their pronounced non-stationary and threshold-based relationships with urban factors using a novel geographically weighted XGBoost (GW-XGBoost) and generalized additive model (GAM) workflow. Our results reveal substantial differences in the spatial patterns of LST and UTCI, along with marked spatial heterogeneity in how 2D and 3D urban factors impact these thermal metrics, as demonstrated by explainable GW-XGBoost models (test R2 = 0.855 for LST and 0.905 for UTCI). Crucially, spatially explicit SHAP shows that sky view factor plays a central role in explaining UTCI variability but exhibits a comparatively marginal independent contribution to LST, indicating that LST inadequately captures shading-driven and radiative processes governing actual human heat stress. Moreover, SHAP-GAM analysis indicates that higher albedo is associated with increased UTCI. These findings provide model-informed planning implications for integrating physiologically relevant thermal indices to support targeted heat risk management and human-centric urban planning.

title: From toxicity to conformity: adaptive user behavior to social norms in Telegram communities
abstract: Toxic and antisocial user behavior on social media platforms has received considerable scholarly attention due to its detrimental effects on society. This study takes a holistic perspective on the phenomenon of online toxicity by investigating the impact of local community norms on toxic expression. By using six large-scale datasets, comprising over 500 million Telegram messages collected between 2015 and 2024, we analyze toxic user behavior across multiple chats and languages. We introduce a methodological framework that uses a conformity index to characterize conformist, anti-conformist, and independent behavioral tendencies. Our findings show that most users tend to conform to local normative environments, aligning their toxicity with the toxicity levels of the chats in which they participate. This pattern is consistent across datasets and languages, showing a strong association between community norms and user behavior online. Furthermore, we observe that higher levels of user participation in chats are associated with a stronger tendency toward conformity with the surrounding social contexts. Collectively, these findings contribute to a deeper understanding of toxic online behavior and highlight the importance of contextualized approaches to content moderation.

title: Making Simulation Accessible; Looking Into Entropy Driven Aggregation of Plates/Flakes in a Colloid Solution
abstract: Computer simulation can reveal how material structure that is otherwise difficult to observe influences properties of a system. Here we consider two simulation questions in parallel: (1) What minimal models are sufficient for observing entropy-driven aggregation in printed inks comprising flakes and polymers? (2) Are there practices that make learning such simulations more accessible to new trainees? We report on coarse-grained models of polymers and flakes and a small subset of observations where flake aggregation is observed. We read literature, participate in programming and version control tutorials, and work individually and in groups on shared simulation tasks like calculating polymer radius of gyration. We find that reading literature provides some of the best opportunity for learning the fundamentals behind the simulations. We describe future potential improvements including simplified polymer representations and deploying simulations on supercomputers.

title: An Investigation into Linking Mammographic and Histology Images
abstract: Breast cancer has a high incidence among women worldwide. Mammography and Hematoxylin & Eosin (H&E) histological images of breast tissue are the two commonly used breast cancer imaging modalities. Among the women who undergo mammographic screening, about 10% are recalled for additional evaluation, while only a few cases referred for biopsy are found to have malignancy, which leads to some unnecessary biopsies. These unnecessary biopsies increase anxiety, morbidity, stress and health care costs. So, the development of a specic discrimination model that could indicate benign abnormalities would reduce this burden. Along with the improvement in medical image analysis, exploring deep learning in the context of mammography and histology image processing has become more realistic. In this thesis, we provide a comprehensive overview of deep learning based methodologies applied to the analysis of mammogramphic and breast histology images. In addition, the relationship between mammography and histopathology phenotypes from a biological point of view is studied. To ll in the gaps in the literature, using well-known convolutional networks, we propose a detection, segmentation and classication model to analyse mammography images and detect mass abnormalities along with classifying them into benign and malignant. Based on our quantitative results, the proposed deeply connected model called DenseNet is able to provide 74.32% classication accuracy on the combination of pre-detected mass abnormalities from various mammographic datasets. From a histological point of view, a deep convolutional network is proposed to detect and quantify mitosis gures in H&E images. The RGB Histogram Specication method to proposed as a pre-processing approach to decrease the sensitivity of the model to stain variations. This model can predict the count of mitoses gures with approximately 80% for F-Score evaluation metric. Along with the aims of this thesis to nd the link between mammography and histology, we propose \the Mammography{Histology{Linking{Model", to provide a mapping of features between mammographic abnormalities and their histopathological representation. This can be addressed in two denitions: (1) retrieving similar samples from repository based on a robust search engine (referred to an retrieval model) and (2) generating histology slides from latent information introduced from mammographic domain to the histology domain (referred to a generative model). The general main aims of these two linking models are to (1) take a mammographic image as input; (2) detect probable mass abnormalities on the whole image; (3) classify the abnormality as benign or malignant and (4) extract a deep abstract (called semantic code). The particular aim of the retrieval model is to associate the extracted abstract to the most appropriate mammographic abstract representation in a data repository and retrieve the top most similar histology images for the query mammographic image. On the other hand, the particular aim of the generative model is to generate a small scale histology image. These two models have never been discussed or developed in the literature and are the most novel parts of this thesis. Challenges for developing such a system are discussed along with the models' potential contribution to clinical decision making and treatment management.

title: Diagnosing Planning Quality in LLM-Based Penetration Testing Using Execution-Free Evaluation
abstract: Evaluating language model (LLM) penetration testing agents through execution conflates planning quality with environmental factors, including network latency, tool failures, and infrastructure variability. Analysis of AutoPenBench logs reveals that 40\% of agent failures arise from environmental timeouts rather than planning errors, obscuring the true diagnostic signal. We present an \textit{execution-free}, rubric-based evaluation framework that directly assesses the quality of LLM-generated attack plans along five independently scored dimensions: tool relevance, sequence logic, completeness, efficiency, and reasoning quality. Ten penetration testing scenarios spanning reconnaissance to post-exploitation are stratified by difficulty and evaluated across four models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.3-70B, and Qwen-2.5-14B—using automated scoring via Claude Sonnet 4.5 at temperature=0. Model scores range from 58\% to 74\%, substantially above the random baseline of 18\% but below the 96\% achieved by expert-generated reference plans, confirming a 78-percentage-point discriminative range. Dimension-level analysis reveals balanced performance across rubric criteria (means 7.0–7.3/10) with notable inter-model variation in efficiency (6.0–7.6) and reasoning quality (5.8–8.1). To strengthen validity, we discuss requirements for human expert validation and inter-rater reliability (target Krippendorff's $\alpha \geq 0.67$), multi-sample generation for variance estimation, and the inclusion of evasion and obfuscation scenarios. The framework offers a reproducible, infrastructure-independent diagnostic tool for model development and security education, intended to complement—not replace—execution-based benchmarks.

title: P_vs_NP
abstract: The P versus NP problem is one of the most celebrated open questions in theoretical computer science and mathematics. This paper attempts to provide an alternative formulation of the problem based on the LFD (Logic–Field–Distribution) real‑domain quantum computing framework. We do not claim a rigorous mathematical proof; instead, we present a conditional perspective: if the postulates of the LFD framework—concerning the real‑number representation of quantum states, the evolution of historical distributions, and the compression operator—are accepted, then the separation of P and NP can be viewed as a natural consequence of a geometric entropy compression speed‑limit theorem. Specifically, we model the solution process of a computational problem as an evolutionary path of an LFD configuration in the geometric tower, and define the computational geometric entropy as the information content of the accumulated historical distribution. We argue that problems in P correspond to those whose computational geometric entropy can be efficiently compressed to a logarithmic scale within polynomial time, whereas NP‑complete problems, due to the inherent branching structure of their solution spaces, possess an incompressible entropy barrier. All background derivations are based on the formal system established in the companion volume Geometric Tower I: Event‑Importance Formulation of Spacetime. The engineering exploration of an LFD‑based meta‑learning system provides qualitative observations consistent with this theoretical picture. This work aims to build a conceptual bridge between computational complexity and the physics of quantum information, and it invites interdisciplinary criticism and discussion.

title: Path-Relaxed Reasoning Optimization for Large Reasoning Models: A Travelling Salesman Problem Relaxation Framework for Structured Inference Training (PRRO-LRM)
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) typically enhance reasoning capabilities in complex tasks by generating long-chain thought processes. However, this "step-by-step unfolding reasoning" is essentially similar to finding a feasible path in an exponentially large state space, resulting in high computational costs and numerous redundant steps. Existing methods often suppress redundant reasoning through truncation, distillation, or external control, neglecting the combinatorial optimization structure of the reasoning path itself. This paper proposes a novel training paradigm: Path-Relaxed Reasoning Optimization (PRRO). This method introduces the relaxation concept from the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) in classical combinatorial optimization into reasoning trajectory modeling. It treats discrete reasoning steps as "reasoning paths" that access semantic state nodes and, through continuous relaxation and dual constraint learning, optimizes "fractional reasoning paths" rather than hard discrete chains during the training phase. This significantly reduces the length of redundant reasoning while maintaining correctness.

title: A Two-Layer Framework for Calibration-Aware Multi-Representation Mathematics Learning Recommendation: Profile Typing and Hierarchical LinUCB
abstract: AI-assisted learning tools are reshaping secondary-school mathematics learning, yet many personalized recommendation pipelines still rely heavily on students’ self-reports [1]. Systematic discrepancies between self-assessed competence and measured performance can degrade recommendation quality [2, 3]. Under the Multiple Representations framework (VIS/SYM/VER/MAN), we align a Likert self-report (1–5) with a 24-item constructed-response assessment (0–5 scoring per item; total 120) and quantify calibration gaps across four representations and twelve conversion pathways. Building on measured ability, calibration bias, preference indicators, and calibration error (MAE), we propose a two-layer model: (i) profile typing via clustering; (ii) hierarchical recommendation that decomposes actions into pathway selection (12 arms) and presentation-mode selection (4 arms), implemented with Hierarchical LinUCB with cold-start warm-up and offline reward shaping. On nine students, the mean MAE_all is 0.333 (median 0.347). Overestimation concentrates on VIS → MAN and MAN → VIS, while underestimation appears on SYM → VIS and VER → SYM. Ablation studies further show how soft preference, continuous leverage, and exploration coefficients affect expected reward and recommendation concentration. The resulting pipeline is reproducible and suitable for iterative online classroom experiments.

title: Construction of a Keyword Extraction Model for Spanish Cultural Elements Based on TextRank
abstract: The deepening application of artificial intelligence in cross-linguistic cultural information processing demands more rigorous algorithms for high-precision cultural element recognition and structured expression. The background stems from the widespread presence of metaphorical expressions, long-range dependencies, and complex cultural entity structures in Spanish texts, which render traditional keyword extraction methods inadequate in terms of semantic consistency and cultural relevance. The objective is to construct a keyword extraction model capable of simultaneously capturing semantic relationships, syntactic structures, and cultural attributes, thereby enhancing the accuracy and stability of cultural element identification. Methodology employs an enhanced TextRank framework. By constructing a culturally enriched semantic graph that integrates semantic similarity, dependency relations, and culturally biased labels, it enables the propagation of multi-source features— —within a unified graph domain. Additionally, a graph signal smoothing mechanism and adaptive iteration strategy are introduced to enhance local structural stability and cross-sentence semantic aggregation capabilities. Results demonstrate significantly superior overall performance compared to baseline models (TF-IDF, original TextRank, PositionRank, KeyBERT) on multi-source Spanish cultural corpora. Improvements are observed across metrics including F1 score, NDCG, and cultural relevance, with markedly enhanced ranking stability for culturally semantically relevant terms. The conclusion highlights that the synergistic design of structured graph modeling and signal processing strategies significantly enhances semantic capture capabilities in cultural texts. This approach provides a reliable technical foundation for cross-lingual cultural knowledge extraction, cultural resource retrieval, and semantic computing framework expansion.

title: How AI Driven Recommendations Shape Purchase Intention in Short Video Commerce on E-Commerce Marketplaces: Evidence from the Mekong Delta, Vietnam
abstract: The focus of the research lies in 5 main perceptions of AI recommendation experience namely AI Recommendation Relevance, AI Serendipity, AI Personalization Fit, Trust in AI Recommendations, and AI Transparency. Data were gathered from a total of 183 consumers through an online questionnaire that was distributed through community groups of users of the E-Commerce marketplaces. The analysis was based on a quantitative procedure that involved the measure of scale reliability via the calculation of Cronbach's alpha, exploratory factor analysis, and multiple linear regression. The results show that the research model is able to explain a significant portion of the variance in Online Purchase Intention. Trust in AI Recommendations The best positive association between trust and purchase intention is in the confidence of algorithmic recommendations in feed based shopping. AI Recommendation Relevance and AI Personalization Fit also show strong positive effects; it seems to be accurate matching and personalization experiences that help consumers to be prepared to buy something. AI Serendipity has a smaller but significant positive relationship with the purchase intention, which shows the effect of useful novelty may be effective in improving shopping motivation at the time of short-video browsing. AI Transparency also contributes to it in a positive way, meaning perceived understandability of the logic behind recommendations has a positive impact on the purchase intention by reducing skepticism and reducing perceived lack of control. The study offers practical implications to marketplace and sellers to optimize the delivery of recommendations and to enhance the shopping experience with short videos for emerging market areas.

title: CognitiveTwin: Robust Multi-Modal Digital Twins for Predicting Cognitive Decline in Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Predicting individual cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD) is difficult due to the heterogeneity of disease progression. Reliable clinical tools require not only high accuracy but also fairness across demographics and robustness to missing data. We present CognitiveTwin, a digital twin framework that predicts patient-specific cognitive trajectories. The model integrates multi-modal longitudinal data (cognitive scores, magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography, cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers, and genetics). We use a Transformer-based architecture to fuse these modalities and a Deep Markov Model to capture temporal dynamics. We trained and evaluated the framework using data from 1,666 patients in the TADPOLE (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) dataset. We assessed the model for prediction error, demographic fairness, and robustness to missing-not-at-random (MNAR) data patterns. ognitiveTwin provides accurate and personalized predictions of cognitive decline. Its demonstrated fairness across patient demographics and resilience to clinical dropout make it a reliable tool for clinical trial enrichment and personalized care planning.

title: Uni-Encoder Meets Multi-Encoders: Representation Before Fusion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing Modalities
abstract: Multimodal MRI offers complementary information for brain tumor segmentation, but clinical scans often lack one or more modalities, which degrades segmentation performance. In this paper, we propose UniME (Uni-Encoder Meets Multi-Encoders), a two-stage heterogeneous method for brain tumor segmentation with missing modalities that reconciles the trade-offs among fine-grained structure capture, cross-modal complementarity modeling, and exploitation of available modalities. The idea is to decouple representation learning from segmentation via a two-stage heterogeneous architecture. Stage 1 pretrains a single ViT Uni-Encoder with masked image modeling to establish a unified representation robust to missing modalities. Stage 2 adds modality-specific CNN Multi-Encoders to extract high-resolution, multi-scale, fine-grained features. We fuse these features with the global representation to produce precise segmentations. Experiments on BraTS 2023 and BraTS 2024 show that UniME outperforms previous methods under incomplete multi-modal scenarios. The code is available at https://github.com/Hooorace-S/UniME

title: Transparent AI in Healthcare: Achieving Dual-Level Interpretability Using Shapley Values
abstract: The integration of machine learning in cardiology offers immense diagnostic potential, yet the "black box" nature of advanced algorithms hinders clinical adoption. Medical professionals require predictive tools that are both highly accurate and strictly interpretable. Clinicians must trust a model’s underlying medical reasoning across diverse populations, while also possessing the ability to explain individual risk assessments to patients. In this project, we developed an XGBoost model using a multi-hospital heart disease dataset and applied SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to achieve full-spectrum clinical transparency. Globally, SHAP feature importance proved the model consistently anchored predictions on biologically sound, universal risk factors—such as asymptomatic chest pain and oldpeak—across entirely different healthcare systems. Locally, SHAP waterfall plots deconstructed individual predictions, translating complex mathematical log-odds into clear, feature-by-feature patient risk profiles. Our findings demonstrate that advanced models need not sacrifice explainability for accuracy. By bridging complex mathematics and actionable clinical insights through dual-level SHAP interpretability, this approach ensures AI can be confidently and safely deployed in real-world healthcare settings.

title: DR v0.3.2: A Blind Adjudication Probe for Delayed Requalification After Valid Update
abstract: Delayed Requalification Probe (DR) v0.3.2 is a compact methods note introducing a blind adjudication protocol for testing whether a model maintains a valid update after a delay and under later requalification pressure. The protocol separates three bounded outcome families: direction maintained, delayed directional erosion, and reference-update mismatch, while also detecting probe invalidity/contamination when the probe structure itself leaks the expected answer. The note documents the locked scoring logic, patch progression, and three blind rounds used to stabilize the protocol. Across these rounds, the protocol converges toward a small, explicit, and reproducible adjudication artifact intended for controlled prompt-based testing rather than broad claims about internal model states. The contribution is methodological: a falsifiable way to distinguish preserved updated direction from later drift or surrogate requalification under delayed conditions. This record includes the methods note and supporting LaTeX source prepared for archival and reuse. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19727067

title: Analysis and Enhancement of Professional Competence of College English Teachers Based on Pattern Recognition Technology
abstract: Artificial intelligence's quick progress has given educators new technology tools for evaluating students' occupational competency. To assess and improve the professional competency of college English teachers (CETs), a multifaceted analytic approach based on pattern recognition (PR) technology is suggested. By integrating multi task cascaded convolutional neural networks (MTCNN) with alpha pose estimation algorithms, automated extraction of teacher facial and pose features has been achieved, and a comprehensive evaluation system has been constructed by combining stacked model fusion algorithms. The outcomes revealed that the accuracy of this method in two datasets is 0.93 and 0.89, respectively, and the F1 scores are 0.93 and 0.90, which are significantly better than traditional one-dimensional evaluation methods. Empirical implementation has demonstrated that the suggested approach can successfully assess instructors' professional competency and offer tailored training suggestions, offering a solid scientific foundation and practical tactics for raising the professional competency of CETs.

title: Deep Learning Model for Early Lung Nodule Classification
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer related mortality worldwide, with about 1.8 million deaths each year, mainly due to late stage diagnosis. Low dose Computed Tomography screening supports early lung nodule detection, but manual review of 200 to 400 CT slices per patient in high volume clinical settings is time consuming and error prone. This study presents a deep learning framework based on transfer learned ResNet50 for automated five class lung cancer classification from axial CT images. The pipeline includes DICOM preprocessing, lung windowing, data augmentation, U Net based lung segmentation, and classification into normal, adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and large cell carcinoma classes. Experimental results on a prepared lung CT dataset show strong and stable classification performance. The model learns discriminative visual patterns from lung tissue and nodules, enabling reliable separation of healthy and cancer affected scans. Evaluation includes class wise performance analysis, confusion matrix assessment, and training convergence analysis to measure generalization across image categories.

title: Neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence for real-time sepsis mortality prediction
abstract: Sepsis mortality prediction in intensive care units represents a critical engineering challenge in healthcare systems, where timely intervention through intelligent decision support systems can significantly reduce mortality rates. Current clinical decision support systems rely on black-box machine learning models that lack the interpretability required for safe deployment in life-critical engineering applications. We develop a neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence framework that integrates Logic Tensor Networks with automated clinical knowledge extraction for interpretable mortality prediction. Our novel contributions include: (1) an automated pipeline for transforming clinical guidelines into first-order logic constraints using medical knowledge graphs and rule mining; (2) a dual axiom architecture with weak anchoring that enables context-adaptive learning while maintaining semantic grounding; and (3) a three-tier explainability framework providing concept-level, rule-level, and patient-level interpretability. Using 19,328 sepsis patients from a publicly available real-world clinical dataset, our system achieves 86.45% accuracy at 6-h prediction windows, outperforming traditional machine learning baselines while providing full transparency in decision-making. External validation on 6735 patients demonstrates preserved ranking ability despite domain shift challenges. • Neuro-symbolic sepsis mortality prediction with 86.45% accuracy and full transparency. • Automated clinical guideline integration via medical knowledge graph and rule mining. • Three-tier explainability framework for concept, rule, and patient-level reasoning. • Outperforms machine learning baselines on sepsis patients. • Addresses artificial intelligence interpretability gap in critical care.

title: PASS: A Provenanced Access Subaccount System for Blockchain Wallets
abstract: Blockchain wallets conventionally follow an ownership model where possession of a private key grants unilateral control. However, this assumption is brittle for emerging settings such as AI agent wallets, organizational custody, and enterprise payroll, where multiple actors must coordinate without exposing secrets or leaking internal activity. We present PASS, a Provenanced Access Subaccount System that replaces role-based or identity-based control with provenance-based control: assets can only be used by subaccounts that can trace custody back to a valid deposit. A simple Inbox-Outbox mechanism ensures all external actions have verifiable lineage, while internal transfers remain private and indistinguishable from ordinary EOAs. We formalize PASS in Lean 4 and prove core invariants, including privacy of internal transfers, asset accessibility, and provenance integrity. We implement a prototype with enclave backends on AWS Nitro Enclaves and dstack Intel TDX, integrate with WalletConnect, and benchmark throughput across wallet operations. These results show that provenance-based wallets are both implementable and efficient. PASS bridges today's gap between strict self-custody and flexible shared access, advancing the design space for practical, privacy-preserving custody.

title: How Hard is it to Decide if a Fact is Relevant to a Query?
abstract: We consider the following fundamental problem: given a database D, Boolean conjunctive query (CQ) q, and fact f in D, decide whether f is relevant to q wrt. D, i.e., does f belong to a minimal subset S of D such that S |= q. Despite being of central importance to query answer explanation, the combined complexity of deciding query relevance has not been studied in detail, leaving open what makes this problem hard, and which restrictions can yield lower complexity. Relevance has already been shown to be harder than query evaluation: namely, $Σ^p_2$-complete for CQs, even over a binary signature. We further observe that NP-hardness applies already to (acyclic) chain CQs. Our work identifies self-joins (multiple atoms with the same relation) as the culprit. Indeed, we prove that if we forbid or bound the occurrence of self-joins, then relevance has the same complexity as query evaluation, namely, NP (without structural restrictions) and LogCFL (for bounded hypertreewidth classes). In the ontology setting, we establish an analogous result for ontology-mediated queries consisting of a CQ and DL-Lite_R ontology, namely that relevance is no harder than query answering provided that we bound the interaction width (which generalizes both self-join width and a recently introduced 'interaction-free' condition). Our results thus pinpoint what makes relevance harder than query evaluation and identify natural classes of queries which admit efficient relevance computation.

title: FixV2W: Correcting Invalid CVE-CWE Mappings with Knowledge Graph Embeddings
abstract: Accurate mapping between Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) and Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) entries is critical for effective vulnerability management and risk assessment. However, public databases, such as the National Vulnerability Database (NVD), suffer from inconsistent and incomplete CVE to CWE mappings, complicating automated analysis and remediation. We introduce FixV2W, a lightweight approach that leverages knowledge graph embeddings and longitudinal trends to improve mapping accuracy of the NVD. FixV2W systematically analyzes historical remapping patterns and leverages hierarchical relationships within NVD and CWE data to predict more precise CWE mappings for vulnerabilities linked to Prohibited or Discouraged categories. We run extensive experimental evaluation of FixV2W, based on test data set collected between August 2021 and December 2024. Considering the Top 10 ranked predictions, the results show that FixV2W predicts the correct CWE mappings for 69% of exploited vulnerabilities that had invalid CWEs before they were exploited. We also show that FixV2W significantly improves the performance of ML models relying on NVD data. For instance, for a model geared at uncovering unknown CVE-CWE mappings, FixV2W improves the Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) from 0.174 to 0.608. These results show that FixV2W is a promising approach to identify and thwart emerging threats.

However, public databases, such as the National Vulnerability Database (NVD), suffer from inconsistent and incomplete CVE to CWE mappings, complicating automated analysis and remediation. We introduce FixV2W, a lightweight approach that leverages knowledge graph embeddings and longitudinal trends to improve mapping accuracy of the NVD. FixV2W systematically analyzes historical remapping patterns and leverages hierarchical relationships within NVD and CWE data to predict more precise CWE mappings for vulnerabilities linked to Prohibited or Discouraged categories. We run extensive experimental evaluation of FixV2W, based on test data set collected between August 2021 and December 2024. Considering the Top 10 ranked predictions, the results show that FixV2W predicts the correct CWE mappings for 69% of exploited vulnerabilities that had invalid CWEs before they were exploited. We also show that FixV2W significantly improves the performance of ML models relying on NVD data. For instance, for a model geared at uncovering unknown CVE-CWE mappings, FixV2W improves the Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) from 0.174 to 0.608. These results show that FixV2W is a promising approach to identify and thwart emerging threats.

title: IdeaCrafter: An Intelligent Machine Learning–Powered Chatbot for Personalized Entrepreneurial Mentorship and Startup Guidance
abstract: ABSTRACT IdeaCrafter is an intelligent AI-based platform designed to provide personalized mentorship for aspiring entrepreneurs through a conversational chatbot interface. In today’s fast-growing startup ecosystem, many individuals struggle to access expert guidance, especially in the early stages of their business journey. This project addresses that gap by offering real-time, data-driven, and context-aware suggestions using machine learning and natural language processing techniques. The system analyzes user inputs such as business ideas, startup stage, and specific requirements, and generates meaningful recommendations related to funding, product validation, and market strategies. It integrates modern technologies including AI models, APIs, and cloud-based databases to ensure scalability, efficiency, and real-time interaction. by combining chatbot intelligence with structured data analysis, IdeaCrafter aims to democratize entrepreneurial mentorship, making it accessible, affordable, and scalable for a wide range of users including students and startup founders. title: Branch-and-Cut Reasoning: A Structural Optimization Paradigm for Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) significantly improve performance on complex tasks by generating long-chain reasoning, but they also introduce problems such as redundant reasoning, path explosion, and computational waste. Existing methods (such as self-regulating tuning) mainly reduce over-reasoning from the perspective of "termination control," but lack the ability to globally optimize the structure of the reasoning space. This paper proposes a novel training/tuning paradigm—Branch-and-Cut Reasoning (BCR). Its core idea comes from the Branch-and-Cut theory in integer programming, but in this work it is redefined as a "structural constraint learning mechanism for the reasoning trajectory space." This paradigm models the reasoning process as a search problem in a high-dimensional discrete path space. It expands multiple candidate reasoning trajectories through "branching" and learns generalizable reasoning constraints through "cutting," thereby dynamically shrinking the ineffective reasoning region. Unlike existing methods, BCR does not simply reduce tokens, but learns the "reasoning feasible region," enabling the model to actively avoid redundant paths during the generation process. This paper proposes a Reasoning Polytope, Semantic Cuts, and an adaptive branching strategy to construct a complete training framework. Theoretically, it is proven that this method can reduce inference complexity from exponential path expansion to convergence under polytopic constraints. This paradigm provides a novel structured learning path for next-generation efficient inference models.
