title: Segmentation-guided knowledge distillation framework for interpretable breast cancer classification
abstract: Abstract Despite the great advances in the clinical diagnosing system, breast cancer is still the most common and fatal disease to woman all over the world, which indicates that there is still a urgent demand of precise and explainable diagnosis system. In this work, we propose a segmentation-guided knowledge distillation framework, which combines the high accuracy of deep learning and clinical explanation ability for breast cancer detection on ultrasound images. The proposed method utilizes a teacher–student framework, and the ResNet-50 teacher is capable of transferring high-level diagnostic representations to the MobileNetV2 student model. Segmentation masks are used as an auxiliary input to guide the student to attend to the tumor areas during training and to improve the relevance of features. This combination provides a good balance for knowledge transfer with low computational complexity. Tested on the BUSI ultrasound dataset, the model outperformed traditional CNN and transfer learning baseline with an overall accuracy and F1-score of 94%. Furthermore, scalability studies demonstrated robust results for reduced fractions of the dataset with real-time inference at more than 200 FPS. The results suggest that distillation of segmentation to the classification task, in the proposed framework improves diagnostic ability and enhances the model explainability, hence it leads to robust and trustworthy AI solutions for breast cancer screening.

title: Some Large Language Models Exhibit Consistent Risk Attitudes
abstract: As artificial intelligence systems are deployed in open-ended, high-stakes settings, a critical dimension remains unmeasured: how perceived risk is translated into action. We test whether large language models (LLMs) exhibit systematic and consistent risk attitudes under uncertainty. We introduce a cross-domain framework that decouples contextual risk belief from categorical decision, and apply it to six representative LLMs and 100 human participants across spatial navigation, clinical triage, and financial allocation tasks. Using regression models, we extract each agents belief-to-decision mapping and quantify risk sensitivity and risk attitude bias. We find that most tested LLMs exhibit (i) robust intra-task consistency, indicating stable mappings from contextual belief to risk decision within a fixed task domain; (ii) cross-domain rank-order stability, preserving relative risk posture across tasks; and (iii) a convergence toward a restricted risk-attitude distribution relative to the broader human baseline. These results reveal risk attitude as a stable and previously uncharacterized dimension of LLM behavior, establishing a foundation for evaluating and aligning AI systems in open-ended decision-making and motivating further investigation into the origins of these intrinsic behavioral dispositions.

title: Noise-Free Quantum Compilation: Structured Output Distributions on NISQ Hardware Without Mitigation
abstract: Author's note — September 2026: I put this paper up during a period when I was overzealous — I'm disabled and I use AI due to my disability, and I was too trusting of a hallucinating model while I was still trying to figure things out. I've learned a great deal since (I'm building my own models now), and I've come back to restrict what doesn't hold up scientifically, leaving up only what's tangible. I apologize for what shouldn't have gone up in the first place. — Richard Vigslist. Experimental results from the NuviraQ quantum circuit compiler demonstrating that structured, repeatable probability distributions can be produced on IBM NISQ hardware without noise mitigation, error correction, post-selection, or variational feedback. Results span 19 tests and 100+ circuit executions across three IBM QPU backends (Fez, Torino, Marrakesh), including multi-peak distributions in 4-qubit harmonic detection and 90% two-state concentration in 8-qubit entangling chains. Cross-backend variance held below 1.1% with 96-hour temporal stability across four IBM calibration cycles. Challenges the prevailing assumption that runtime mitigation is a prerequisite for structured output on current quantum hardware.

title: Automated Quantum Error Correction Code Selection via Noise Profile Analysis: Bias Detection, Correlation Awareness, and Resource-Optimal Recommendation
abstract: Selecting the optimal QEC code requires expertise in both hardware noise and multiple code families. We present an automated engine that takes raw error rates, classifies noise, detects bias (Z/X asymmetry ratio) and correlated burst errors, and recommends the optimal code with minimum distance and resource estimate. The decision tree maps Z-biased noise to repetition codes, correlated burst noise to color codes, very low rates to Steane codes, and general noise to surface codes. Integration with FTQC resource estimation provides total physical overhead. We demonstrate up to 52.5x reduction in physical qubit count compared to default surface code selection when noise exhibits strong bias.

title: Data Large Model Analysis Framework Driven by Causal Modeling and Experimental Validation
abstract: To address the problems of low analytical efficiency, insufficiently intuitive reasoning logic, and low credibility of analytical results in traditional data analysis methods when handling cross-domain and multi-source heterogeneous data, this paper proposes a large-model analysis framework constrained by structural causal graphs. The framework deeply integrates domain causal rules into the model reasoning process, thereby achieving positive guidance and effective control over the direction of reasoning. A comparative experiment is conducted using a simulated unmanned aerial vehicle reconnaissance effectiveness attribution analysis scenario. The experimental results verify that the proposed framework can effectively reduce the uncertainty of large models in complex causal reasoning tasks and significantly improve the reliability and interpretability of analytical results. The proposed method provides an interpretable intelligent enhancement technical pathway for the automated analysis of cross-domain and multi-source heterogeneous data.

title: Design of an Adaptive Knowledge Structure Constructing Method for Advanced Mathematics Based on Generative Intelligence
abstract: Fixed representations of sophisticated mathematics knowledge cannot fully capture the hierarchical relationships, pre-requisite relationships and individual differences related to cognition of learners. In order to solvei this problem, this study proposes an adaptive construction method of knowledge structure based on generative intelligence. The proposed method combines ontology-based knowledge encoding, symbolic expression representation, graph dynamic updating and multi-source learning behavior analysis. Simultaneous modeling of concept relations and learner mastery states using a structural space that contains math concepts, formulas, answers to exercises, learning trajectories, dwell time and error patterns. Based on this, the node association, edge weight, weak knowledge connection and personalized learning path are dynamically reconstructed. The experimental results reveal that the proposed method can obtain 90.8% accuracy, 3.2% higher than GKT and 12.3% higher than BKT method. The improvement of learning is 18.1%, the completion time and cognitive load are reduced, compared to conventional learning paths. The results show that the method promotes the adaptability of the structure, weak nodes identification, and can effectively support the intelligent instructional intervention of complex mathematical knowledge system and personalized advanced learning.

title: Image Sentiment Analysis Algorithms and Public Opinion Guidance in Visual Communication
abstract: Addressing the challenges of quantifying image affective information and the lag in public opinion guidance within visual communication, this study constructs a multi-level affective analysis algorithm integrating ResNet and Transformer. The approach incorporates hierarchical feature extraction, including low-level visual encoding, mid-level semantic parsing, and high-level sentiment embedding, allowing more explicit modeling of emotional cues embedded in visual content. Furthermore, a dynamic regression mechanism is employed to capture the temporal coupling between sentiment fluctuations and public opinion intensity, while a risk threshold–based regulation model enables adaptive intervention strategies under rapidly evolving opinion dynamics. Experiments conducted on AffectNet and T4SA datasets (62,400 total samples) demonstrate 92.4% recognition accuracy and an F1 score of 91.3%, representing a 6.6% improvement over traditional architectures. Testing within real-world public opinion scenarios further confirms the model's capability to suppress negative sentiment propagation through iterative adjustment of dissemination rhythm and semantic restructuring. Negative sentiment diffusion rates decreased by 22%, and fluctuations in opinion intensity reduced by 19%. Overall, the integration of sentiment recognition, temporal prediction, and risk-driven regulation forms a closed-loop framework that enhances the stability, interpretability, and responsiveness of sentiment management in visual communication environments.

title: GR: a fixed-frequency time series data timestamp compression algorithm based on RLE
abstract: The existing time-series data compression algorithms do not fully consider the specific case of time-series data with fixed frequency. When the time-series data is compressed, the general compression algorithms are still used, resulting in a certain degree of information redundancy. Based on this, a GR (Gorilla_RLE) timestamp compression algorithm for fixed frequency sequential data is proposed based on Gorilla compression algorithm. First, obtain the first order differential value of the timestamp of each data point; Then, obtain the second order differential value of the timestamp, and adopt a corresponding compression strategy based on the data distribution of the second order differential value; Finally, RLE encoding is performed on consecutive and identical second-order difference values. Experiments on publicly available datasets show that the proposed method can compress the timestamp of fixed frequency sequential data more effectively than Gorilla and other compression algorithms, and the larger the fixed frequency sequential dataset, the higher the compression rate.

title: Emotion Detection from Text Using TF-IDF and Logistic Regression: A Hybrid NLP Framework with Real-Time Deployment
abstract: Sentiment analysis is critical to text mining due to rapid text data growth. Sentiment analysis is utilized to track social media, rate customer opinions, diagnose mental diseases, and understand how humans talk to computers. Most emotion-detecting methods today center around non-text inputs, but come on, much of what we learn about humans online is text-based. Therefore, the goal of this project is to develop a system with AI that detects emotions from text. The proposed system uses natural language processing (NLP) techniques and machine learning models to classify emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, fear, and surprise, among others, from textual input.. It incorporates rule-based methods, sentiment, and context-sensitive tools aiding emotion detection. It employs some incredible advanced natural language processing technology such as sentence transformers, and BERT-like models to accurately pin down neutral sentiments Evaluation metrics, including accuracy, F1 score, and recall, demonstrate the effectiveness of the model, highlighting its potential for real-world deployment. The findings suggest that AI-based emotion analysis from text holds promise for improving human-computer interaction and enabling more emotionally responsive applications They test it on public sentiment analysis corpora, and the experiments prove that our model is better than current approaches in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall. This just shows how great AI-based emotion analysis is inimproving the way we communicate with computers and creating apps that can understand emotions.

title: How Supply Chain Dependencies Complicate Bias Measurement and Accountability Attribution in AI Hiring Applications
abstract: The increasing adoption of AI systems in hiring has raised concerns about algorithmic bias and accountability, prompting regulatory responses including the EU AI Act, NYC Local Law 144, and Colorado's AI Act. While existing research examines bias through technical or regulatory lenses, both perspectives overlook a fundamental challenge: modern AI hiring systems operate within complex supply chains where responsibility fragments across data vendors, model developers, platform providers, and deploying organizations. This paper investigates how these dependency chains complicate bias evaluation and accountability attribution. Drawing on literature review and regulatory analysis, we demonstrate that fragmented responsibilities create two critical problems. First, bias emerges from component interactions rather than isolated elements, yet proprietary configurations prevent integrated evaluation. A resume parser may function without bias independently but contribute to discrimination when integrated with specific ranking algorithms and filtering thresholds. Second, information asymmetries mean deploying organizations bear legal responsibility without technical visibility into vendor-supplied algorithms, while vendors control implementations without meaningful disclosure requirements. Each stakeholder may believe they are compliant; nevertheless, the integrated system may produce biased outcomes. Analysis of implementation ambiguities reveals these challenges in practice. We propose multi-layered interventions including system-level audits, vendor guidelines, continuous monitoring mechanisms, and documentation across dependency chains. Our findings reveal that effective governance requires coordinated action across technical, organizational, and regulatory domains to establish meaningful accountability in distributed development environments.

title: Robust Fuzzy local k-plane clustering with mixture distance of hinge loss and L1 norm
abstract: K-plane clustering (KPC), hyperplane clustering, and mixture regression all essentially fall within the same class of problems. This problem can be conceptualized as clustering in relatively high-dimensional K subspaces or K linear manifolds. Traditional KPC or fuzzy KPC models demonstrate a pronounced susceptibility to outliers, as they presuppose that the projection distance between data points and the plane normal vector adheres to the L2 distance. Meanwhile, the assumption of infinitely extending clusters adversely affects clustering performance. To solve these problems, this paper proposed a new robust fuzzy local k-plane clustering (RFLkPC) method that combines the mixture distance of hinge loss and L1 norm. The RFLkPC model assumes that each plane cluster is bounded to a finite area, which can flexibly and robustly handle plane clustering tasks with outliers or not. The corresponding model and optimization algorithms of RFLkPC were provided. Compared to other related models on this topic, a large number of experiments verify the efficiency of RFLkPC on simulated data and real data. The source code for the proposed RFLkPC method is publicly available at https://github.com/xuelin-xie/RFLkPC.

title: Learning Reactive Human Motion Generation from Paired Interaction Data Using Transformer-Based Models
abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have enabled the generation of videos from textual descriptions as well as the prediction of future sequences from input videos. Similarly, in human motion modeling, motions can be generated from text or predicted from a single person's motion sequence. However, these approaches primarily focus on single-agent motion generation. In contrast, this study addresses the problem of generating the motion of one person based on the motion of another in interaction scenarios, where the two motions are mutually dependent. We construct a dataset of paired action-reaction motion sequences extracted from boxing match videos and investigate the effectiveness of Transformer-based models for this task. Specifically, we implement and compare three models: a simple Transformer, iTransformer, and Crossformer. In addition, we introduce a person ID embedding to explicitly distinguish between individuals, enabling the model to maintain structural consistency and better capture interaction dynamics. Experimental results show that the simple Transformer can generate plausible interaction-aware motions without suffering from posture collapse, while iTransformer and Crossformer accumulate errors over time, leading to unstable motion generation. Furthermore, the proposed person ID embedding contributes to preventing structural collapse and improving motion consistency. These results highlight the importance of explicitly modeling individual identity in interaction-aware motion generation.

title: Neuro-Edu: A Cognitive Science-Driven Framework for Large Language Model Alignment in Educational Sandbox Simulation
abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in educational contexts demands a fundamental reconceptualization of alignment methodologies, moving beyond generic helpfulness optimization toward pedagogically-grounded cognitive alignment. This technical whitepaper presents Neuro-Edu, a comprehensive framework that synthesizes principles from cognitive science—specifically cognitive load theory, dual-process reasoning models, self-regulated learning theory, and schema theory—with state-of-the-art LLM alignment techniques to create adaptive educational sandbox simulations. Unlike prior approaches that treat alignment as an orthogonal concern to educational effectiveness, Neuro-Edu operationalizes cognitive science principles as explicit alignment objectives, enabling LLMs to dynamically calibrate explanation complexity based on real-time cognitive load estimation, promote both intuitive and analytical reasoning through systematic scaffolding strategies, and support progressive transfer of regulatory control from system to learner. Extensive experiments across mathematical reasoning, scientific explanation, and programming education domains demonstrate that Neuro-Edu achieves statistically significant improvements over baseline alignment approaches, with a 47.3% increase in knowledge retention rates, 69.2% improvement in transfer learning outcomes, and 55.1% enhancement in metacognitive engagement scores. title: Cultural Anchor Loss and Related Failure Patterns in Large Language Models: Evidence from Spanish Popular Culture
abstract: This paper introduces Cultural Anchor Loss (CAL) as a distinct failure mode in large language models, separate from factual hallucination. CAL occurs when a model fails to detect that a given expression either lacks a single unambiguous referent or requires specific cultural anchoring beyond statistical association. Instead of suspending judgment and requesting clarification, the model produces a confident, plausible, but incorrect response. We present empirical evidence from a structured evaluation of 12 cases drawn from Spanish popular culture (music lyrics, advertising slogans, television catchphrases, and real broadcast events), tested against GPT-4.5 and GPT-5. We also describe a taxonomy of ten related phenomena observed during the evaluation, of which Cultural Anchor Loss is proposed as the primary failure mode from which several others derive.Este artículo introduce la Pérdida de Anclaje Cultural (Cultural Anchor Loss, CAL) como un modo de fallo específico en los modelos de lenguaje de gran escala, distinto de la alucinación factual. El CAL se produce cuando un modelo no detecta que una expresión dada carece de un referente unívoco o requiere un anclaje cultural específico más allá de la asociación estadística. En lugar de suspender el juicio y solicitar aclaración, el modelo produce una respuesta segura, plausible pero incorrecta. Se presenta evidencia empírica a partir de una evaluación estructurada de 12 casos extraídos de la cultura popular española, probados con GPT-4.5 y GPT-5, junto con una taxonomía de diez fenómenos relacionados.

title: Audio Processing Techniques for Voice Cloning and Information Extraction from Audio Files
abstract: Voice cloning has become a rapidly evolving field in artificial intelligence and speech processing. Recent advances in deep learning have made it possible to replicate human voices with remarkable accuracy using relatively small datasets. At the core of this technology lies the ability to analyze and interpret audio signals in order to capture the unique characteristics of a speaker’s voice. Audio files contain a wide range of information including speech content, speaker identity, emotional state, pronunciation patterns, and environmental context. Extracting and modeling this information is essential for developing effective voice cloning systems. Modern voice synthesis frameworks rely on several stages of audio signal processing including signal acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction, representation learning, and neural speech generation. This paper presents a comprehensive study of how audio signals are processed in voice cloning systems and explores the various types of information that can be extracted from audio recordings. The research examines the structure of digital audio signals, the methods used to convert sound waves into machine-readable data, and the feature extraction techniques that capture acoustic properties of speech. In addition, the paper investigates modern neural architectures used for voice cloning such as spectrogram-based models, neural vocoders, and speaker embedding networks. The study also highlights several practical applications of voice cloning technologies including digital assistants, personalized speech synthesis, accessibility tools, and entertainment systems. Furthermore, the research discusses ethical considerations and potential risks associated with voice cloning technologies, emphasizing the need for responsible development and robust detection mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that audio signals contain rich multi-layered information that can be effectively utilized to develop advanced speech synthesis and analysis systems

title: A Multi-Layer Security Defense Framework for Industrial Intelligence
abstract: The rapid evolution of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is reshaping industrial cybersecurity. While generative artificial intelligence enables defense capabilities such as threat detection, vulnerability mining, and security operations, it also introduces new risks through malicious uses like automated attacks and deepfakes. Existing studies often focus on a single dimension, lacking systematic analysis of full-lifecycle risks and holistic defense strategies for industrial scenarios. This paper proposes a five-dimensional risk framework covering computing power, data, model, application, and compliance governance, along with a matching three-layer collaborative defense system of technology, management, and governance, offering theoretical and practical guidance for industrial risk prevention in the GAI era.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Affect Aware Content Adaptation in Intelligent Tutoring Systems
abstract: Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) have advanced in personalized learning, but their ability to adapt to learners' emotional states is limited. This paper proposes an emotion-aware content adaptation framework using Reinforcement Learning (RL). A lightweight CNN extracts facial expressions and emotional features from video streams, which are then integrated with cognitive data. A Deep Q-Network (DQN) dynamically adjusts content difficulty, presentation, and pacing to enhance long-term learning outcomes. This approach enables personalized learning experiences based on students' emotional states (such as frustration or boredom), making intelligent tutoring systems more interactive and adaptive, thereby enhancing students' emotional satisfaction and long-term learning outcomes. This framework offers a novel solution for emotion-driven adaptive teaching in intelligent tutoring systems.

title: A Review of Large Language Models for Cybersecurity Defense: Core Capabilities, Application Practices, and Challenges
abstract: The rapid evolution of cyber threats — characterized by advanced persistent threats (APTs), software supply chain attacks, and AI-driven adversarial payloads — has exposed fundamental limitations in traditional rule-based and signature-based defense mechanisms. Large Language Models (LLMs), with core capabilities spanning natural language understanding, code engineering, logical reasoning, and autonomous decision-making, offer a transformative paradigm for cybersecurity defense. This paper presents a systematic review of LLM applications across the entire cybersecurity defense lifecycle. The review begins with an analysis of the core capabilities and key enabling technologies of LLMs — including prompt engineering, domain fine-tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and agent frameworks — that underpin their adaptation to security tasks. Application practices are then examined across four critical stages: pre-attack prevention and secure development (covering vulnerability detection, secure code generation, supply chain security, and malware/phishing detection), during-attack detection and threat awareness (including network intrusion detection, log analysis, and threat intelligence automation), post-attack response and disposition (encompassing digital forensics and automated incident response),. The paper further dissects the security risks inherent to LLMs themselves — such as prompt injection, jailbreaking, data poisoning, and model stealing attacks — along with corresponding defense technologies. Finally, key challenges are identified, including hallucination, real-time performance bottlenecks, domain knowledge scarcity, data silos, interpretability deficits, and compliance risks, with future research directions proposed toward building more robust, trustworthy, and human-centered intelligent defense systems.

title: Prompt-Based Emotion Detection and Story Generation
abstract: Emotion recognition from text and story generation with aligned emotions are still difficult tasks in natural language processing because of the imbalance problem, the overlap of emotions, and the open-ended nature of creative text generation. This paper proposes a hierarchical emotion-aware framework that combines super-sentiment classification, fine-grained emotion recognition, data augmentation, and story generation based on prompts in a single pipeline. The proposed system involves three-class super-sentiment classification and fine-grained emotion recognition using RoBERTa-based transformer models trained on the EmpatheticDialogues dataset. To handle the imbalance problem, a controlled data augmentation approach that leverages paraphrasing, back translation, and semantic filtering is used. Experimental results show that the proposed super-sentiment classifier has an accuracy of 71.86%, and the ablation study validates the effectiveness of the hierarchical labeling approach and controlled data augmentation. The predicted emotional states are then used with a GPT-2 language model using structured prompt conditioning for story generation with aligned emotions without any additional fine-tuning. A discussion on computational complexity and generative evaluation underscores the feasibility and limitations of the proposed framework. The proposed architecture effectively integrates emotion understanding and creative text generation for emotion-aware NLP applications.

title: Artificial intelligence enhances cancer cell selection for HER2 gene amplification assessment in breast carcinoma
abstract: The evaluation of HER2 gene amplification is a time-consuming process that requires quantifying a large number of signals in cancer cells to ensure reproducible results, a task that can be assisted by image analysis (IA) tools. This study aimed to develop and validate an artificial intelligence-based cancer cell detection model for detecting breast carcinoma in bright-field in situ hybridization (ISH) whole-slide images, with the goal of improving cancer cell selection prior to the quantification of HER2 and CEP17 gene copies. The difference in IA performance was not statistically significant compared to visual assessment in quantifying the HER2/CEP17 ratio and average HER2 copy numbers per cell. However, IA with the Cancer Cell Detection Module (IA 2.0) quantified consistently higher values than IA without (IA 1.0). Cancer cell detection in IA 1.0 showed 64% sensitivity, 83% specificity, and a positive predictive value (PPV) above 95% for samples with at least 84% cancer cellularity. IA 2.0 improved cancer cell detection sensitivity to 69% and specificity to 93%, achieving a PPV above 95% for samples with at least 66% cancer cellularity. IA 2.0 showed 95% concordance with visual scoring (k = 0.90), with 90% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Discordant cases required the selection of a second cancer cell-enriched region of interest, shifting classification from HER2-negative to HER2-positive. After correction, IA 2.0 achieved full agreement with visual classification (100%, k = 1.000), underscoring the critical role of the pathologist supervision in this assay.

title: StackFeat RL: Reinforcement Learning over Iterative Dual Criterion Feature Selection for Stable Biomarker Discovery
abstract: Feature selection in high-dimensional genomic data ($d \gg n$) demands methods that are simultaneously accurate, sparse, and stable. Existing approaches either require manual threshold specification (mRMR, stability selection), produce unstable selections under data perturbation (Lasso, Boruta), or ignore biological structure entirely. We introduce StackFeat-RL, a meta-learning framework that optimises the hyperparameters of an iterative dual-criterion feature selection algorithm via REINFORCE policy gradients. The dual criterion, requiring both coefficient consistency and selection frequency, guards against two failure modes missed by single-criterion methods, while iterative accumulation provides convergence guarantees via the law of large numbers. On COVID-19 miRNA data (GSE240888, 332 features) and three Alzheimer's disease classification tasks (GSE84422, 13237 genes; Normal vs.\ Possible, Probable, and Definite AD), StackFeat-RL achieves the highest predictive accuracy among all evaluated methods, including ElasticNet, Boruta, mRMR, and stability selection, while requiring 3--4$\times$ fewer features. Keywords: feature selection, reinforcement learning, REINFORCE, elastic net, biomarker discovery, Alzheimer's disease, dual-criterion selection, protein interaction networks

title: BERAG: Bayesian Ensemble Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering
abstract: A common approach to question answering with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is to concatenate documents into a single context and pass it to a language model to generate an answer. While simple, this strategy can obscure the contribution of individual documents, making attribution difficult and contributing to the ``lost-in-the-middle'' effect, where relevant information in long contexts is overlooked. Concatenation also scales poorly: computational cost grows quadratically with context length, a problem that becomes especially severe when the context includes visual data, as in visual question answering. Attempts to mitigate these issues by limiting context length can further restrict performance by preventing models from benefiting from the improved recall offered by deeper retrieval. We propose Bayesian Ensemble Retrieval-Augmented Generation (BERAG), along with Bayesian Ensemble Fine-Tuning (BEFT), as a RAG framework in which language models are conditioned on individual retrieved documents rather than a single combined context. BERAG treats document posterior probabilities as ensemble weights and updates them token by token using Bayes' rule during generation. This approach enables probabilistic re-ranking, parallel memory usage, and clear attribution of document contribution, making it well-suited for large document collections. We evaluate BERAG and BEFT primarily on knowledge-based visual question answering tasks, where models must reason over long, imperfect retrieval lists. The results show substantial improvements over standard RAG, including strong gains on Document Visual Question Answering and multimodal needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks. We also demonstrate that BERAG mitigates the ``lost-in-the-middle'' effect. The document posterior can be used to detect insufficient grounding and trigger deflection, while document pruning enables faster decoding than standard RAG.

title: SAMIDARE: Advanced Tracking-by-Segmentation for Dense Scenarios
abstract: Automated sports analysis demands robust multi-object tracking (MOT), yet segmentation-based methods often struggle with mask errors and ID switches in dense scenes. We propose SAMIDARE, a framework that enhances SAM2MOT for crowded scenes through three key components: (1) density-aware mask re-generation and (2) selective memory updates, both for adaptive mask control to preserve target feature integrity, and (3) state-aware association and new track initialization, which improves robustness under mutual occlusions and frequent frame-out events. Evaluated on the SportsMOT dataset, SAMIDARE achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming the baseline by 2.5 HOTA and 4.2 IDF1 points on the validation set. These results demonstrate that adaptive feature management using mask control and state-aware association provide a robust and efficient solution for dense sports tracking. Code is available at https://github.com/ZabuZabuZabu/SAMIDARE

title: Desenvolvimento de Confiança e Perseverança em Robótica Educacional com Aprendizagem Baseada em Projetos
abstract: Este artigo apresenta os resultados de um programa de robótica educacional voltado a estudantes do ensino fundamental da rede pública, desenvolvido com a metodologia de Aprendizagem Baseada em Projetos (ABP). As oficinas buscaram promover o desenvolvimento de competências em programação, eletrônica e construção de robôs, além de investigar os efeitos sobre a confiança e a perseverança dos participantes. A pesquisa foi conduzida com abordagem mista (qualitativa e quantitativa), por meio de questionários aplicados ao longo das atividades. Os resultados apontaram aumento na autoeficácia dos estudantes em circuitos eletrônicos e programação, e estabilidade na construção de estruturas físicas e mecânicas. O uso de recursos como protocolos, rubricas, mini-lições e webquests contribuiu para o engajamento e para a consolidação do aprendizado. O programa demonstrou potencial para aproximar a educação tecnológica da comunidade escolar e estimular o interesse pela continuidade dos estudos em cursos técnicos integrados.

title: Gauberte Fabricio de Vagad, el antiguo autor de la Celestina.
abstract: Análisis Estilométrico del Manuscrito II-1520: Autoría y Atribución en el Taller de Zaragoza (ca. 1498): Gauberte Fabricio de Vagad Descripción (Abstract) Este repositorio contiene los resultados y la metodología del estudio estilométrico realizado sobre el manuscrito II-1520 de la Biblioteca de Palacio, empleando el software JGAAP (Java Graphical Authorship Attribution Program). La investigación aplica el algoritmo de Burrows Delta sobre n-gramas de caracteres ($n=6$) y un análisis de los 200 eventos más frecuentes para desentrañar la compleja red de autoría oculta tras las atribuciones tradicionales del siglo XV. Los datos obtenidos demuestran una convergencia estadística irrefutable hacia la figura de Gauberte Fabricio de Vagad y el círculo de la Oficina de los Lucena en Zaragoza. Los resultados sitúan a Vagad como el arquitecto sintáctico del texto, escoltado por un joven Fernández de Oviedo, cuyo perfil actúa como alumno aventajado y ejecutor estilístico dentro del taller de Paulo Hurus. El estudio revela una estructura de "escuela de escritura" donde la sofisticación humanista (reflejada en la proximidad con el control de Bembo) desplaza definitivamente la autoría administrativa de Fernando de Rojas, quien aparece en posiciones de marginalidad estadística (puesto 22, $\Delta > 250$). Este hallazgo es fundamental para la historiografía literaria, ya que identifica el manuscrito II-1520 como el eslabón perdido entre la tradición de Juan de Mena y la modernidad renacentista, gestada en los laboratorios de prosa de la Corona de Aragón. Metodología y Herramientas Software: JGAAP (Burrows Delta). Parámetros: N-gramas de 6 caracteres, 200 eventos más comunes, normalización de espacios en blanco y unificación de mayúsculas. Corpus de Referencia: Perfiles maestros de Fernández de Oviedo, Gauberte Fabricio de Vagad, Luis de Lucena, Hernán Núñez el Pinciano y otros autores contemporáneos del periodo 1470-1530. Fuente Primaria: Transcripción paleográfica del Manuscrito II-1520 (Biblioteca de Palacio).

title: Heisenberg Limited Liquid Networks: Solver‑Free Neural Dynamics via Phase‑Space Uncertainty
abstract: We propose Heisenberg-Limited Liquid Networks (HLLN 2.1), a recurrent neural architecture that achieves continuous-time, liquid dynamics without numerical ODE solvers. By grounding state updates in a learnable uncertainty principle, the network modulates its own temporal integration rate in response to input surprise. HLLN 2.1 uses 75–80% fewer parameters than Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) while matching or exceeding performance on chaotic time-series forecasting, regime-shift adaptation, and character-level language modelling. The architecture exposes an interpretable “Metabolic Friction” signal that correlates with environmental instability, providing built-in uncertainty quantification. All code is available at github.com/Kshitiz-Maurya/HLLN2.1.

title: Construction of an AI-Enabled Evaluation Model for Ideological and Political Course Teaching Effect Based on Machine Learning and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP)
abstract: This paper focuses on the evaluation of teaching effectiveness in ideological and political courses. In response to the limitations of traditional evaluation methods and combined with the application trend of AI technology in the field of education, it constructs an AI-enabled evaluation model for ideological and political course teaching effectiveness based on machine learning and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Firstly, it introduces the basic principles of machine learning, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and its advantages, as well as the relevant theoretical foundations of the teaching effectiveness evaluation system. Secondly, it elaborates on the model design ideas, including the principles and basis for constructing the evaluation index system, the AHP-based weight allocation method, and the process of data collection and preprocessing. Then, by comparing and analyzing different machine learning algorithms, it selects the final algorithm, expounds the parameter tuning strategy, builds the experimental environment, details the experimental procedure, and visualizes and interprets the results. Next, it demonstrates the application of the model in actual teaching scenarios through case analysis, compares teaching effectiveness before and after application, collects and analyzes student feedback, and discusses the challenges encountered in the implementation process and corresponding countermeasures. Finally, it summarizes the research findings, reviews the main conclusions, explains the significance of this study for the reform of ideological and political course teaching, points out the deficiencies of the current model, and proposes future improvement plans and broader application prospects.

title: Intelligent Analysis System of College Students' Behavior Based on Data Mining
abstract: With the continuous construction of the smart campus system, colleges and universities have put forward higher intelligent and personalized requirements for student behavior management and services. However, the current intelligent perception and control technology has significant deficiencies in the continuity of behavior data collection, the accuracy of behavior pattern recognition, the dynamic update capability of individual portraits, and the real-time nature of resource recommendation, making it difficult to meet the diversified development needs of students. To this end, this paper proposes to deeply integrate artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things to build an intelligent analysis system for college student behavior. The system collects multi-dimensional data such as students' card access, library stay time, canteen consumption frequency, dormitory return time, and teaching building entry and exit behavior in real time through Internet of Things devices, and combines K-means clustering, principal component analysis (PCA) and long short-term memory network (LSTM) to model behavioral characteristics and predict trends. Based on the above model results, an adaptive recommendation engine is further designed to accurately push personalized course resources, work and rest improvement suggestions, and campus activity notifications based on students' learning preferences and behavioral habits. Experimental results show that after introducing the AIoT fusion model, the frequency of student library use increases by 28.7% compared with the baseline, the utilization rate of course resources increases by 26.7%, the frequency of late return behavior decreases by 22.4%, and the click-through rate of recommended content reaches 42.3%, achieving high-resolution identification of student behavior and refined improvement of university services.

The system collects multi-dimensional data such as students' card access, library stay time, canteen consumption frequency, dormitory return time, and teaching building entry and exit behavior in real time through Internet of Things devices, and combines K-means clustering, principal component analysis (PCA) and long short-term memory network (LSTM) to model behavioral characteristics and predict trends. Based on the above model results, an adaptive recommendation engine is further designed to accurately push personalized course resources, work and rest improvement suggestions, and campus activity notifications based on students' learning preferences and behavioral habits. Experimental results show that after introducing the AIoT fusion model, the frequency of student library use increases by 28.7% compared with the baseline, the utilization rate of course resources increases by 26.7%, the frequency of late return behavior decreases by 22.4%, and the click-through rate of recommended content reaches 42.3%, achieving high-resolution identification of student behavior and refined improvement of university services.

title: Smaller, Younger, and More Impactful: How AI-Assisted Writing Transforms Research Teams
abstract: The era of Big Science has long been defined by increasingly large and specialized research teams pushing the frontiers of knowledge. However, recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), are beginning to reshape academic writing and scientific research, potentially disrupting the longstanding trend toward ever-larger teams and transforming other dimensions of research team structure. Drawing on 147,074 full-text publications from the PLoS family and the Nature portfolio since 2020, we examined whether and how AI-assisted writing influences team structure and team outcomes in science. Using multiple methods, including ordinary least square, quantile regression, Poisson regression, logistic regression and propensity score matching, we found that research teams using AI-assisted writing tend to be younger and smaller. Importantly, this shift toward more compact, junior-leaning teams does not come at the expense of scientific impact. On the contrary, we observed a higher probability of research teams that employed AI-assisted writing producing highly impactful publications. These results highlight the significant role of AI-assisted writing in reshaping not only how research is produced, but also how research teams are formed and assembled. Our findings call for policy improvements in research evaluation, funding, and training to address this emerging trend.

title: Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair
abstract: There is a rapidly growing interest in using Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate complex network operations, but their reliable adoption requires rigorous assessment of their effectiveness and safety. Existing benchmarks do not address whether LLMs can successfully resolve errors in large-scale, interdependent network configurations without introducing new disruptions. Developing such a benchmark is challenging: scenarios must be diverse and increasingly complex, yet their evaluation must be straightforward and meaningful. In this paper, we present Cornetto, the first benchmark to evaluate LLM-driven network configuration repair functionally and at scale. Cornetto features a generation pipeline that synthesizes representative and plausible misconfiguration scenarios, coupled with an evaluation framework that uses formal verification to assess functional correctness of proposed fixes against ground-truth specifications. Using this pipeline, we synthesize a dataset of 231 problems for fixing configurations across varying network topologies (20--754 nodes) and diverse protocols. We evaluate 9 state-of-the-art LLMs and find that while they show promise, they often introduce regressions and their performance degrades at scale. Our results indicate that reliable LLM-powered network automation requires integrating LLMs into iterative workflows guided by formal verification.

title: Logistic Bandits with $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{dT})$ Regret without Context Diversity Assumptions
abstract: We study the $K$-armed logistic bandit problem, where at each round, the agent observes $K$ feature vectors associated with $K$ actions. Existing approaches that achieve a rate-optimal $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{dT})$ regret bound rely heavily on context diversity assumptions, such as strict positivity of the minimum eigenvalue of a context covariance matrix. These assumptions, however, impose strong restrictions on the context process, as they rule out the situation where the context vectors are concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace. In this paper, we propose SupSplitLog, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first algorithm for logistic bandits that achieves $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{dT})$ regret without any context diversity assumption. The key idea is to split the collected samples into two disjoint subsets when constructing estimators; one is used to compute an initial-point estimator, while the other is used to apply a Newton-type one-step correction procedure. The splitting rule is carefully designed to balance the accuracy requirements of the initial-point estimator and the one-step correction procedure. Moreover, SupSplitLog strictly improves on the existing algorithms in terms of the dependence on dimension $d$ in the regret upper bound. Furthermore, SupSplitLog can be adapted simply to deduce a regret bound that grows with a data-dependent complexity measure, avoiding a direct dependence on $d$, which is favorable when the context vectors are concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace. We also provide experimental results that demonstrate numerically the superiority of our algorithm, validating the theoretical results.

title: Energy-Efficient Federated Learning with Temporal Convolutional Networks for Intrusion Detection
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has significantly increased the attack surface of modern network infrastructures, necessitating intelligent and scalable intrusion detection systems. Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for distributed model training without centralized data sharing; however, challenges such as energy efficiency, data heterogeneity, and privacy preservation remain inadequately addressed. Existing studies often emphasize optimization objectives theoretically without validating them under realistic constraints. This paper proposes an energy-aware federated learning framework integrating Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) for intrusion detection using distributed network traffic data. The framework incorporates differential privacy for secure model updates and a conceptual energy-aware client participation strategy. Experiments are conducted on the UNSW-NB15 dataset under a controlled setting with fixed client participation and communication parameters. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves improved classification accuracy and stable convergence behavior across communication rounds while operating under a fixed energy budget. However, energy consumption remains constant due to controlled experimental conditions, indicating that the study evaluates performance under energy constraints rather than dynamic energy optimization. The findings highlight the effectiveness of TCN-based federated models for intrusion detection in resource-constrained environments. Future work will focus on dynamic energy modeling, heterogeneous client environments, and comprehensive multi-objective evaluation.

title: The underlying logic and innovative development path of artificial intelligence technology
abstract: Since the beginning of the 21st century, artificial intelligence technology has developed at an unprecedented speed, gradually permeating into every aspect of our lives, from voice assistants on smartphones to autonomous vehicles, from medical diagnosis to financial analysis. Artificial intelligence has become an important force driving social progress. Artificial intelligence may seem both familiar and mysterious. We use the conveniences it brings every day, but rarely delve into its underlying logic and innovative development path. In fact, the development of artificial intelligence is not achieved overnight, but is built upon a complex and stable technical system, simultaneously influenced by various factors such as market demand, policy guidance, and ethical constraints. A deep understanding of the underlying logic and development path of artificial intelligence not only helps us better adapt to future society but also stimulates our interest and contemplation in technological innovation. With the continuous evolution of technology, artificial intelligence is no longer just a concept in scientists’ laboratories, but has truly entered thousands of households and become an indispensable part of modern life. It has changed our learning methods, communication modes, and even ways of thinking, and its influence is continuously expanding.

title: Artifact: Tool Paper: AGTix: Concise Definition of Scope Graphs in Reference Attribute Grammars
abstract: This artifact accompanies the tool paper 'AGTix: Concise Definition of Scope Graphs in Reference Attribute Grammars' of Luke Bessant and Eric Van Wyk, submitted to ACM SIGPLAN SLE 2026. Its purpose is to demonstrate the use of AGTix constructs for specifying the construction and interrogation of scope graphs, which are implemented as a language extension to the reference attribute grammar language Silver. AGTix is a fusion of Statix (inspiration for the constructs introduced is primarily inspired by MiniStatix) and reference attribute grammars (Silver specifically), which brings Statix-like constraints for building and querying scope graphs into RAGs as new equation forms, implemented as a language extension to Silver. This allows a much more concise definition of scope graph-based name analysis than is yielded by the full Statix-to-RAGs translation of our previous work. The new AGTix constructs implicitly translate to attribute declarations/definitions and production equations akin to what is presented in that previous work, hiding the details such as how targets of edge assertions are propagated around an AST, which often involve many more equations and definitions than what AGTix specifications yield. It also means that Statix specifications can be more easily translated to RAG specifications, as a consequence of AGTix is that these now have a much closer line-to-line correspondence. The artifact contains a number of example languages with name resolution semantics defined using AGTix, scripts for compiling those languages, and other scripts for executing each with test input programs which compare output against expected results. Packaged with this artifact are the Silver Jarfiles for the latest version of AGTix.

title: Unified Quantum-Safe Security Platform with Noise Reachability Analysis and Enhanced QKD Eavesdrop Detection
abstract: We present QCrypton v4.0, extending the unified quantum-safe security platform with two major capabilities: (1) a Quantum Noise Reachability Engine that classifies noise into 12 sub-types, evaluates against 6 QEC codes (720 evaluations), and recommends optimal correction with 24 compensating controls; and (2) enhanced BB84 eavesdrop detection via statistical noise decomposition, demonstrated catching an eavesdropper at 9.8 sigma when standard BB84 reported "secure." The platform now comprises 12 scanners, post-quantum crypto (FIPS 203/204/205), FTQC cost estimation (28 algorithms), noise reachability, code scanning (6 languages), and automated remediation — all via CLI/SDK/API with zero third-party crypto dependencies.

title: Reward-Guided Dynamic Fusion and Modality Decoupling for Enhanced Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) integrates multiple modalities to better understand human emotions. However, existing methods often neglect heterogeneity among modal features, causing redundancy and inconsistencies. Additionally, the dynamic interplay between modalities is frequently ignored during fusion, limiting performance. To address these issues, we propose Reward-Guided Dynamic Fusion and Modality Decoupling (RDFD). RDFD includes two key components: (1) a feature decoupling module that separates modality-specific and modality-shared features, reducing redundancy and conflicts; (2) a Reward-Guided Dynamic Fusion module that adaptively selects guiding modalities to enhance modality-specific representations and enable flexible fusion. Experiments on the CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI datasets show that RDFD achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in advancing Multimodal Sentiment Analysis.

title: Assessing Machine Translations of Advertising Slogans: A Pilot Study with Human Evaluation and BLEURT Scores
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have made significant advancements in natural language processing tasks, particularly in translations. Existent studies have explored their performance in translation of domains such as idioms, however, there is limited research which focuses on translation of advertising slogans. This pilot study aims to investigate the feasibility of applying DeepSeek-V3.2 in translation of skincare product slogans and evaluate the model performance when it is instructed with four prompt templates. The evaluation is conducted by two practicing translators supplemented by the automatic metric BLEURT. The findings suggest improvement in translation qualities with the prompts as measured by human judgement. Preliminary evidence suggests that translation outputs could be better than others when prompts include consumer information, though the observation remains tentative. However, according to BLEURT scores, the model could perform better than baseline-prompted translations only when instructed with prompts consisting of brand names. Significant divergences in their rankings reflect discrepancies between evaluation criteria of human annotators who prioritize cultural adaptability and linguistic appropriateness, and BLEURT which focuses on semantic similarities and fluency.

title: Design and Application of Intelligent Feedback System for English Writing Based on BERT and Learning Analytics
abstract: Aiming at the problems of heavy manual correction workload, strong subjectivity, and delayed feedback in college English writing teaching under the background of educational digitalization, this paper designs and implements an intelligent writing feedback system based on BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) and learning analytics. The system constructs a rigorous multi-dimensional feature engineering framework, which explicitly extracts and quantifies lexical features (e.g., type-token ratio), syntactic features (e.g., sentence complexity), discourse coherence, and semantic completeness. To ensure methodological rigor, this study conducts three layers of experimental verification: a large-scale model comparison experiment, an ablation study to validate feature design, and a 16-week controlled teaching quasi-experiment with statistical significance tests. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed BERT-based model achieves an accuracy of 92.4%, which is significantly superior to traditional machine learning baselines. In the teaching experiment, the group using the proposed system achieved a 12.5% increase in writing scores and a 53.8% reduction in grammatical errors (p<0.001). The system provides a feasible technical solution for the digital transformation of English writing evaluation.

title: A Computational Approach to Service Quality Mining in Mobile Reading Applications Using LDA Topic Modeling and SnowNLP Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This study presents an integrated computational framework combining Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling and SnowNLP sentiment analysis to systematically mine service quality insights from Chinese user reviews of mobile reading applications. We collected 7,991 reviews from three major platforms operating under different business models (Tomato Novel, QiMao, Qidian) via the Tencent MyApp marketplace and applied systematic text preprocessing including jieba word segmentation, part-of-speech tagging, and stopword removal, yielding 4,741 valid samples (59.3% retention rate). The LDA model with optimized hyperparameters (α=0.1, β=0.01, k=5) achieved excellent coherence (C_v=0.5430), identifying five service dimensions: Payment/Monetization (47.6%), Advertising (21.7%), Content Ecosystem (19.8%), Content Quality (6.1%), and Authors (4.8%). Notably, business model topics dominate user attention (69.3% vs 30.7% content-related), challenging the traditional "content is king" paradigm. Sentiment analysis revealed 60.8% positive reviews (mean=0.6261), with advertising showing surprisingly positive sentiment (0.73, 72.7% positive rate), suggesting user acceptance of ad-supported free models. Cross-platform comparison demonstrates Tomato's ad-supported model (0.7252) significantly outperforms QiMao's hybrid (0.5017) and Qidian's premium subscription (0.4967) approaches. This framework demonstrates unsupervised text mining efficacy for service quality assessment and provides actionable insights including optimal ad frequency (1-2 ads/chapter) and duration (5-15 seconds) thresholds for platform optimization.

title: Soil Data Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Large Language Models
abstract: Abstract This study examines the applicability of large language models for automated data extraction from soil-science research papers, using a corpus of Russian-language articles from the journal Pochvovedenie/Eurasian Soil Science (2019–2020). Extraction quality was evaluated using GPT-4 Turbo’s answers to a set of 58 questions covering characteristics of research objects and conditions, soil types, measurement methods, and measurement results. Automated and expert-based approaches to assessing the correctness of the model’s answers were compared. The aim was to evaluate how well large language models (LLMs) can extract and verify data from scientific articles. The baseline model’s outputs were compared with expert gold-standard annotations, deterministic metrics based on lexical overlap, and the scores of several alternative language models acting as independent “judges.” The integrated F1 score for individual questions was at least 0.73, while the mean values across thematic question groups reached 0.91–0.99. The correlation between the most consistent judge model Gemini 2.5 Flash and expert ratings reached 0.8 and explained about 60% of the variance in expert assessments, whereas classical n-gram metrics were significantly less informative. These results indicate that LLMs are promising as the basis of a scalable pipeline for the automated construction of soil property databases and reducing manual effort in the analysis of scientific texts.

title: Attention-Based Deep Learning for Medical Insurance Cost Prediction: A Comparative Analysis of TabNet and Tabular Transformers
abstract: We need accurate estimates of healthcare insurance costs so that we can set fair prices and use our resources wisely. The lack of use of attention-based methods in the study of healthcare tabular data, even though they have great potential, makes premium valuation models less accurate and harder to understand. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of attention-based models in comparison to conventional baseline models for forecasting medical insurance costs. We used 1338 de-identified health insurance information to test five models: linear regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, as well as TabNet and a Tabular transformer. We used the root mean squared error and the coefficient of determination to see how well it worked. A notable finding from the analysis of the results is that about 60.69 percent of the total significance is due to smoking-related factors. In conclusion, the suggested research utilizing attention-based models offers interpretability advantages that are beneficial in healthcare settings and comparable to strong tree-based standards. The analysis and forecasts that come from this are helpful for making decisions and setting prices in a clear way.

title: A Specialized Importance-Aware Quantum Convolutional Neural Network with Ring-Topology (IA-QCNN) for MGMT Promoter Methylation Prediction in Glioblastoma
abstract: GBM is a highly aggressive primary malignancy in adults, necessitating personalized therapeutic strategies due to its inherent molecular heterogeneity. MGMT promoter methylation is a pivotal prognostic biomarker for anticipating response to temozolomide-based chemotherapy. Although various AI frameworks have been developed for non-invasive MGMT prediction, spatial heterogeneity of methylation status and the high-dimensional and correlated nature of MRI data frequently constrain discriminative feature learning and generalizability of classical models. To circumvent these limitations, a specialized IA-QCNN architecture is proposed, based on the principles of quantum mechanics, including superposition and entanglement, and enabling more efficient representation learning in high-dimensional Hilbert space. The framework establishes a methodological bridge between GBM radiogenomics and quantum deep learning by integrating energy-based slice selection, importance-aware weighting, ring-topology quantum convolution, and folding-based pooling layers. When the model predicts MGMT promoter methylation status using both mpMRI and T1Gd images, experimental results demonstrate that the IA-QCNN achieves high accuracy despite its low number of trainable parameters while effectively minimizing the overfitting problem observed in classical models. Quantitative analyses reveal that the T1Gd modality possesses higher discriminative power than mpMRI, establishing a clinically significant sequence preference. Furthermore, the model exhibits exceptional robustness in hybrid noise environments, effectively utilizing noise as a regularization mechanism to enhance predictive performance. Consequently, the specialized IA-QCNN architecture provides a robust and computationally efficient alternative to classical approaches in the analysis of heterogeneous radiogenomic data.

title: Iterative Model-Learning Scheme via Gaussian Processes for Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of (Semi-)Batch Processes
abstract: Batch processes are inherently transient and typically nonlinear, motivating nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC). However, adopting NMPC is hindered by the cost and unavailability of dynamic models. Thus, we propose to use Gaussian Processes (GP) in a model-learning NMPC scheme (GP-MLMPC) for batch processes. We initialize the GP-MLMPC using data from a single initial trajectory, e.g., from a PI controller. We iteratively apply the NMPC embedded with GPs to run batches and update the GP with new observations from each iteration, thereby achieving batch-wise improvements. Using uncertainty quantification from the GPs, we formulate chance constraints to enforce safe operation to the required confidence levels. We demonstrate our approach in \textit{silico} on a semi-batch polymerization reactor for tracking and economic objectives over durations of two hours, and the reactor temperature is constrained in a range of $\pm2^\circ C$ around its setpoint. After only four batch iterations, tracking error from the GP-MLMPC scheme converged to a reduction of $83\%$, compared to the initial trajectory. Furthermore, under an economic objective, the GP-MLMPC resulted in a 17-fold increase in final product mass by iteration 8, compared to the initial trajectory. In both cases, the resulting GP-MLMPC performance is on par with the full-model NMPC, which shows that the optimal controller can be learned by the approach. By collecting samples around the optimal trajectory, the GP-MLMPC remains sample-efficient across iterations and achieves quick convergence. Thus, the proposed GP-MLMPC scheme presents a promising data-efficient approach for the control of nonlinear batch processes without mechanistic knowledge.

title: SS-MOM-XAI: A Responsible AI Governance Framework for AI-enabled Service Ecosystem (AISE)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in AISE, extending from user encounters to organisational coordination and institutional oversight. In such layered structures, explanation failures cannot be reduced to algorithmic opacity alone; rather, they often arise from sociotechnical misalignments among AI-mediated decision-making, organisational responsibilities, and accountability structures. To address this gap, this study proposes SS-MOM-XAI as a methodological framework for operational human-centred AI in AISE. The framework reframes explainability from a modular property to distributed AI governance in service. The SS-MOM-XAI comprises five core components: SS architecture, MOM hierarchy, approach taxonomy, analytical framework, and product-service design method. Empirically, the framework is applied to two contrasting ecosystems: the Fresh Flower Retail Delivery Service Ecosystem (FFRDSE) and the Bluetooth Charging Service Ecosystem for New Energy Vehicles (BCSEfNEV). Cross-case findings indicated that governance depth increases with domain risk and that explanation obligations must be distributed across service layers. The study makes the following main contributions: it proposes the SS-MOM-XAI framework for human-centred AI in AISE. It provides systematic guidance for analysing and designing for understandability in real service ecosystems. Furthermore, provides an implementation strategy with actionable recommendations through a three-phase model that spans the design projects.

title: PEDAGOGICAL MODEL FOR MANAGING INDIVIDUAL EDUCATIONAL DIRECTIONS BASED ON INTERACTIVE PEDAGOGICAL SOFTWARE TOOLS
abstract: This article covers the theoretical and practical foundations of managing students' individual educational programs (IEDs) using interactive pedagogical software tools (IPDQ). It is substantiated that the modern educational paradigm requires a personality-oriented approach, which, in turn, leads to the need to adapt the content of education to the needs, abilities, and pace of assimilation of the student. Based on the analysis of the architecture of adaptive learning systems, foreign (RWTHmoodle, FLIC) and national platforms, the article proposes a pedagogical model for designing ITB through IPDQ.

title: MCFS: LLM Reasoning Method Based on Multi-Level Constraints and Multi-Source Fusion Beam Search
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have exhibited strong capabilities in language understanding and generation for open-domain question answering. However, they still suffer from widespread knowledge scarcity and hallucination issues in multi-hop factual reasoning scenarios, which affect the accuracy of reasoning results. The Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG) paradigm can effectively make up for this defect and improve the reliability and interpretability of generated answers. Nevertheless, existing KG-RAG methods have obvious limitations: they either ignore the importance of graph structural information or neglect the relevance between relations and question semantics, ultimately restricting the accuracy of multi-hop reasoning. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces MCFS, an LLM reasoning method that integrates multi-level constraints with multi-source fusion beam search, whose core goal is to achieve effective alignment among question semantics, LLM prior knowledge, and graph structural information. Specifically, first, we innovatively propose to generate multi-level constraints based on LLMs, providing precise guidance by extracting semantic constraints from questions; second, we train a semantically guided edge-level graph neural network (GNN) to model relation relevance; then, we innovatively propose a multi-source fusion beam search strategy to explore reliable reasoning paths; finally, we leverage explicit reasoning paths to guide LLMs in generating interpretable answers. Experimental results on standard knowledge graph question answering benchmarks show that MCFS consistently outperforms strong baselines and delivers the best overall performance.

title: Empathetic Gamified Feedback for English Learners: A Lightweight Reward Calculator with Dynamic Sentiment Adaptation
abstract: This paper propose a novel Reward Calculator system that generates empathetic, gamified feedback for English learners while minimizing data dependency. The system integrates psycholinguistic analysis with lightweight transformer models and reinforcement learning to dynamically adapt feedback based on real-time emotional and linguistic cues. Unlike conventional approaches, our method avoids extensive user profiling by employing a sentiment-aware analyzer to extract emotional valence and linguistic complexity, which then condition a dynamic reward generator to produce human-like responses. Furthermore, the system embeds gamification directly into the reward calculus, enabling seamless progression tracking without auxiliary modules. The proposed architecture combines DistilBERT for efficient sentiment analysis and GPT-2 Small for feedback generation, ensuring scalability and low-latency interaction. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves higher emotional resonance and linguistic accuracy compared to static reward functions. This work bridges the gap between affective computing and language learning, offering a practical solution for real-time conversational practice with minimal data overhead. The approach is particularly significant for applications where user privacy and computational efficiency are critical constraints.

title: Research on Topic Modeling and Evolution Analysis of Sci-tech Literature Based on Multi-data Source Fusion
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has demonstrated strong potential in the fields of text mining and knowledge discovery. The core issues currently faced by the topic modeling and evolution analysis of scientific and technological literature include shallow semantic understanding, difficulty in multi-source fusion, low topic quality, rough evolution analysis, low computational efficiency, and insufficient cross-language support. This study proposes a framework for topic modeling and evolution analysis of scientific and technological literature based on multi-source data fusion. By introducing Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers for Topic Modeling In addition to BERTopic, it combines cross-source mid-term fusion strategies to enhance topic consistency, interpretability, and the accuracy of evolution tracking. The experimental results show that the topic consistency score of the proposed method on the literature dataset in the field of artificial intelligence reaches 0.71, and the topic diversity is 0.89. Compared with the traditional Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model method, it is improved by more than 40%. And after expert verification, it successfully identified emerging frontier topics such as "AI-enabled scientific discovery" and "neuro-symbol fusion". Overall, this framework has achieved effective improvements in the accuracy of topic discovery and the reliability of evolution tracking. It provides an effective intelligent analysis solution for scientific research trend detection and decision support.

title: Cognitive-aware dual-state fusion network for knowledge tracing
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) aims to predict students’ future performance by analyzing their learning records. Although existing deep learning-based KT models have achieved notable progress in inferring students’ knowledge states and forecasting upcoming performance, it remains challenging to model learners’ behaviors and cognitive processes with sufficient granularity. This paper proposes CaDSKT (Cognitive-aware dual-state fusion network for knowledge tracing), leveraging deep learning techniques to achieve more comprehensive and accurate estimation of learners’ cognitive states. Specifically, the authors design a dedicated deep representation module for problem-solving states and introduce a hybrid attention mechanism (parallel–fusion) to effectively capture complex cognitive dynamics throughout the learning process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model substantially outperforms existing approaches in prediction accuracy and knowledge-state modeling capability. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness and synergy of the individual components.

title: A Multimodal Deep Learning Approach for Emotion-Aware Speech Recognition
abstract: The following research proposes an integrated Deep Learning pipeline that unifies speech recognition, natural language understanding, and emotion-aware analysis to achieve human-like comprehension of spoken interactions. The system initiates with the fine-tuning of OpenAI's Whisper model by LoRA-based parameter-efficient training on the LibriSpeech ASR dataset for high-quality, lightweight speech-to-text transcription. The model performance was evaluated against metrics such as WER, CER, and BLEU score for linguistic fidelity. Subsequently, the resultant text is subjected to several steps involved in a multi-stage Natural Language Processing framework about Glove embedding, an Autoencoder, and then a Bidirectional GRU-based RNN for extractive summarisations, while a Keyword CNN highlights semantically important terms. The most relevant sentences, identified by the RNN, are passed to advanced transformer models such as Google Gemini and T5 for abstractive summarization, yielding coherent, context-rich summaries of conversations. In parallel, the system includes an emotion recognition module trained on the RAVDESS dataset using MFCC features extracted with torch audio and modelled through both MLP and GRU architectures. By analyzing pitch variation and RMS energy, the system maps detected emotions into expressive "vibe" categories such as enthusiastic, frustrated, hesitant, or calm, providing an additional emotional layer to dialogue understanding. Together, these components create a comprehensive AI framework capable of transcribing speech, understanding its semantic essence, summarizing key information, and interpreting emotional tone, forming a foundation for the next generation of emotionally intelligent and context-aware conversational systems.

title: GenMatter: Perceiving Physical Objects with Generative Matter Models
abstract: Human visual perception offers valuable insights for understanding computational principles of motion-based scene interpretation. Humans robustly detect and segment moving entities that constitute independently moveable chunks of matter, whether observing sparse moving dots, textured surfaces, or naturalistic scenes. In contrast, existing computer vision systems lack a unified approach that works across these diverse settings. Inspired by principles of human perception, we propose a generative model that hierarchically groups low-level motion cues and high-level appearance features into particles (small Gaussians representing local matter), and groups particles into clusters capturing coherently and independently moveable physical entities. We develop a hardware-accelerated inference algorithm based on parallelized block Gibbs sampling to recover stable particle motion and groupings. Our model operates on different kinds of inputs (random dots, stylized textures, or naturalistic RGB video), enabling it to work across settings where biological vision succeeds but existing computer vision approaches do not. We validate this unified framework across three domains: on 2D random dot kinematograms, our approach captures human object perception including graded uncertainty across ambiguous conditions; on a Gestalt-inspired dataset of camouflaged rotating objects, our approach recovers correct 3D structure from motion and thereby accurate 2D object segmentation; and on naturalistic RGB videos, our model tracks the moving 3D matter that makes up deforming objects, enabling robust object-level scene understanding. This work thus establishes a general framework for motion-based perception grounded in principles of human vision.

title: Quantum interference of distinguishable photons based on spatially resolved measurements
abstract: We present experimental results demonstrating the quantum interference of two photons distinguishable in their transverse momenta, each entering the input ports of a balanced beam splitter. This counterintuitive interference effect is made possible through spatially resolved measurements in the near field, i.e., by resolving the conjugate variable in which the photons are distinguishable. Our experimental findings agree with theoretical predictions. We contrast our results with a non-spatially resolved measurement where averaging over the photons' positions washes out the quantum interference observed in spatially resolved measurements.
